title: inbox: hermes inbox as a labs plugin (from hermes-agent #81507)
body:
`hermes inbox` as a labs plugin, ported from hermes-agent PR #81507 (Cursor-inspired "everything in flight" view) with no core changes.

## What it does
`hermes inbox [--json]` prints, for the active profile: **Needs attention** (failed/paused cron jobs, stalled or dropped delegations, orphaned background processes, blocked/review kanban tasks), **In progress** (live background processes, running delegations, running kanban tasks), **Finished, not yet delivered**, **Scheduled** (next cron runs), **Open surfaces** (live chat sessions with titles), and a **Not read** footer naming any source that was absent/unreadable.

## Data sources (read-only)
| Source | How |
|---|---|
| `processes.json` | file read; host PIDs re-checked with psutil |
| `state.db` → `async_delegations` | sqlite `mode=ro`, 2 s busy timeout |
| `cron/jobs.json` | file read (utf-8-sig) |
| `runtime/active_sessions.json` | file read (current `{"entries": [...]}` shape + legacy list); PID + start-time liveness; titles via `SessionDB(read_only=True)` |
| kanban | current board's `kanban.db`, resolved by the documented `HERMES_KANBAN_*` / `kanban/current` rules, sqlite `mode=ro` |

Changes vs the PR: the PR read the lease file as a bare list, but current core writes `{"entries": [...]}`, so open surfaces would always be empty; fixed and covered by a test that takes a real lease through core's registry. Kanban and session titles are new. Multi-line cron errors are collapsed to one line. No private core imports (`plugins validate` gives no rule-9 warning). Pending approvals are skipped (they only exist in the asking process's memory), and the README says so.

## Verification
- `python -m pytest -q` → 29 passed. The tests seed a temp HERMES_HOME through core's own writers (SessionDB, kanban init_db/create_board, the active-session registry), check board resolution against core's `kanban_db_path`, and check that building the inbox leaves every store byte-identical.
- `hermes plugins validate inbox` → passed
- Real run against a scratch home seeded with the cron CLI (including a real failed `--no-agent` script run), SessionDB sessions, live lease holders, a kanban task blocked via `hermes kanban block`, plus hand-written process-checkpoint and delegation rows. The output is in the README. Also ran against an empty home (all clear, sources listed as absent, no files created) and with `hermes -p work inbox` (profile cron shown, shared kanban board).

title: fix(record): a secret `autocomplete` token in a list is a secret field
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two fixes to the workflow recorder, both about secrets in recordings.

**1. A secret `autocomplete` token in a list was not recognised as a secret field.**

`autocomplete` is a space-separated token list in HTML, so a field marked `autocomplete="username current-password"` (or `"section-login one-time-code"`) holds a secret. Both sides compared the **whole attribute string** against the secret names instead of its tokens, so such a field was not seen as a secret:

- the recorder JS read its value, so the raw secret crossed the CDP socket;
- the Python masking pass missed it too, so the plaintext value was written into the recording file under `~/.hermes/recordings/`.

The rule is now one token-list pattern, shared by the recorder JS and the Python pass, so the two cannot drift apart again — the plugin masks twice on purpose, and the two halves have to agree. The plain value never reaches the recording, and the field keeps its name in the `{SECRET:<name>}` placeholder.

**2. A recording is owner-only.**

The directory and the file are created 0700/0600. A recording holds what the user typed — a password the masking missed, an API key typed into a plain field, the prompts and URLs themselves — and neither may be readable by another local account.

## Why it matters

A recording is a file the agent later reads back as a workflow, so a plaintext password in it is a credential on disk and in the model's context (and from there in a provider's logs). The markup that triggers it (`autocomplete="username current-password"`) is the pattern the HTML spec recommends for grouped login fields, and what Rails/Django/Angular forms emit.

## Tests

- `tests/test_recording.py`: 9 new cases — a secret token among others is masked, a list without a secret token is not, the case/whitespace variants, the recorder JS pinned to the *same* rule as the Python pass, and the owner-only modes (POSIX only).
- Red on base: the new cases fail without the change (the value comes back as `s3cr3t` instead of `{SECRET:f}`).
- The plugin's suite: 84 passed, 1 skipped (the modes test is POSIX-only).

title: fix: owner-only plugin state, parameterized SQL, precise recorder tab docs
body:
﻿## What does this PR do?

Three hardening fixes from a full audit of the repo (all three plugins' source read; every suite run against current Hermes core on Python 3.13). It does not overlap with #3, which fixes the recorder's secret masking ΓÇö this PR touches no \\workflow-record\\ code, only its README.

**1. telegram-business: the plugin state store is owner-only.**
\\\state.db\\ holds the customer conversation and the drafts the owner approved. The directory and the SQLite file are now created 0700/0600 (best-effort, POSIX; a no-op on Windows where \\\~/.hermes\\\ already sits inside an ACL-protected profile). Same rationale as #3's recordings fix; \\\_restrict_to_owner\\\ is the same shape so both plugins behave identically.

- \\\	ests/test_business_mode.py\\\: one new case (POSIX-only, skipped on Windows) asserting file and directory modes.
- README gains a **Safety properties** bullet.

**2. inbox: the live delegation states travel as bound parameters.**
\\\collect_delegations\\\ built \\\'running'\\\, \\\'finalizing'\\\, \\\'stalling'\\\ inside the SQL string. The tuple is a constant, so nothing was injectable ΓÇö but it was the only f-string interpolation into a query in the repo, and \\\LIVE_DELEGATION_STATES\\\ is shared (imported by report.py). Now all three placeholders are bound parameters like every other query value; the result is byte-for-byte identical rows.

**3. workflow-record: README only ΓÇö how the recorded tab is chosen.**
CDP exposes no notion of \\\ rontmost\\\, so the recorder takes the browser's *first web-page tab* (\\\pick_page_target\\\), which with several tabs open may differ from the tab you are looking at. The README said \\\keep that tab in front\\\, which oversells what the recorder can do; both the Record step and the One tab limit now state the real rule.

## Why it matters

1. keeps private conversation text (and any secret a customer happened to type in a business chat) out of other local accounts on shared POSIX systems; 2. removes the one query-construction pattern that could silently become injectable if a state name ever came from data; 3. documents a real selection rule so a first-time user does not record the wrong tab.

## Tests

- \\\	elegram-business\\\: 44 passed, 1 skipped (the mode test is POSIX-only) ΓÇö was 44 passed.
- \\\inbox\\\: 29 passed, behavior unchanged.
- \\\workflow-record\\\: 74 passed (README-only change; suite rerun to be sure).
- Red on base: the new telegram-business case fails without the change (\\\


## Addendum (second commit): the draft TTL is now enforced

Investigating further surfaced that `expire_telegram_business_drafts()` existed, was tested, and was never invoked by any runtime path — and `handle_callback` only checked `status == 'pending'`. A pending draft's buttons (Send included) stayed actionable forever, against the README's safety claim that stale buttons no-op after the 24h TTL.

- `handle_callback` re-checks `expires_at` before dispatching a choice and settles aged-out drafts as expired.
- `maybe_handle_edit_capture` re-checks it before an override send (the owner can sit on the "send me the text" prompt arbitrarily long).
- Three new tests pin the behavior: stale Send no-ops, an aged-out edit override is refused, and a control proves a fresh Send is never rejected.
- README: the bullet now states how the TTL is enforced, and the hard-coded "37 tests" count (44 by then, 48 now) became wording that cannot drift.

telegram-business suite: 47 passed, 1 skipped (the POSIX-only mode test).

title: Adopt: inbox
body:
I'd like to adopt Inbox.

I run Hermes as an always-on personal assistant on a Mac mini (gateway, cron jobs, kanban workers, delegations), and Inbox is the one view I want for what's stuck or waiting. I plan to wire it into my agent's morning self-check via `hermes inbox --json` and retire my own overlapping collectors, so it will get daily use.

What I'd take on: keep it working against current Hermes with tests on nightly, triage and fix issues, and send SHA-bump PRs to the catalog entry under the usual rules.

Happy to move it to github.com/ZK-Snarky/hermes-inbox (or wherever you prefer) and point plugin-catalog/inbox.yaml at it. Thanks for putting these up for adoption.

title: ci(tests): install hermes-agent through uv with its override-dependencies
body:
The nightly `tests` run on `main` went red on 2026-10-23 for every plugin at "Install hermes-agent": pip stops with `ResolutionImpossible` because core pins `Pillow==13.0.0` while its dependency browser-harness pins `pillow==12.3.0`. Core settles that conflict with `[tool.uv] override-dependencies`, which pip ignores. Open PRs #3 and #4 are red for the same reason, not their code.

This installs core and each plugin's dependencies through uv with core's override list, the same change hermes-official-plugins#163 made there.

- Before: nightly run on `main` 2026-10-23, every job fails at the install step (`hermes-agent 0.0.0 depends on Pillow==13.0.0` / `browser-harness 0.1.13 depends on pillow==12.3.0`).
- After: this PR's own `tests` run, all plugins on Linux, macOS and Windows.

title: feat(inbox): add durable observations, local attention and Herald threads
body:
## Summary

Extend the existing `inbox` plugin with durable observations and local attention management. This is the upstream implementation route requested in the review of NousResearch/hermes-agent#143572, rather than a competing catalog entry.

The manifest stays `inbox`, the command stays `hermes inbox`, and the existing Labs identity, licenses and release process are retained.

### Added

- Explicit `observe`, independent `changes`/`mark-seen` consumers, and an atomic profile-local SQLite observation store.
- Occurrence-scoped `ack` and bounded `snooze`. Changed observations and expired snoozes resurface without resolving the native task.
- Opt-in same-host Herald aggregation and work threads joined by exact trace/parent IDs, with source coverage and truncation disclosed.
- Conservative attention lanes that keep execution, accepted outcome, delivery, evidence and local attention distinct. Missing facts stay unknown; classification grants no execution permission.

### Boundaries

Ordinary views remain read-only. Explicit state actions write only `<profile-home>/inbox/state.db`; native task and dispatch databases remain read-only. No network, subprocesses, telemetry, background polling, automatic retries, credential reads or approval changes are introduced.

The port is based on current Labs main `6a72dfdf45d2a7e20e0c54843b0496c6ed94f53c`. It preserves the upstream parameterized delegation-state query, including when recent delivered completions are requested. Other Labs plugins, CI, artwork and licenses are unchanged. Outside `inbox/`, the only edit is the Inbox description in the root README.

### Verification

- **143 tests passed locally** against the native Hermes runtime, including the existing suite and two additional bound-SQL regressions for both completion-window modes.
- Both new regressions fail against the earlier fork implementation and pass in this upstream port.
- Native plugin validator: **15 checks passed, security scan safe, zero warnings**.
- The source implementation being ported previously passed 141 tests on each of Linux, macOS and Windows, plus isolated native installation and a short real-task pilot: https://github.com/RohiRIK/hermes-inbox/actions/runs/39960423916
- The two upstream-port regressions have been executed locally on Linux; this PR's CI is the independent cross-platform gate. A longer normal-work soak is not claimed.

The published fork revision used as the source is `87597329c2fa3634183ca187ad89ccbcebc553dc`. This PR removes fork-specific naming/install copy and keeps the upstream plugin identity. After upstream review/merge, the existing `inbox` catalog entry can be advanced through its normal reviewed SHA bump; this PR does not change the catalog pin or any live installation.

title: fix(business): a double-tapped Send no longer delivers the reply twice
body:
## Problem

`BusinessModeManager.handle_callback` reads the draft's `pending` status and *then* awaits the customer send. Two Send taps on the same draft that arrive while the first send is in flight both pass the status check, both call `send_message`, and the customer receives the approved reply **twice**. The second `resolve_…` then no-ops silently, so the owner's screen looks correct while the contact has a duplicate.

Same shape for the Edit tap plus an immediate Send, or a double-tap on a laggy phone.

## Fix

One in-flight claim per draft:

- `self._send_inflight: set[int]`; the SEND branch claims `draft_id` synchronously after the status/owner checks (no await between check and claim, so it is race-free under the single event loop).
- A second tap on a claimed draft answers `⏳ Already sending that draft.` and stops.
- The claim is released in a `finally`, so a *failed* send (row still `pending`) can be retried from the same buttons.

Edit and Discard need no claim: both persist their state change before their first await.

## Test

`test_double_tap_send_delivers_once` drives two overlapping callbacks against a send stub that parks the customer send on an `asyncio.Event`:

- exactly one customer-chat send,
- the loser gets the "already sending" answer,
- the draft ends `sent`.

Fails before the change (two customer sends), passes after.

title: fix(business): one junk config value no longer disables Business Mode
body:
## Problem

`register()` coerced four config values with bare `float()`/`int()`. ``plugins.entries.telegram-business`` lives in a hand-edited `config.yaml`, and one typo there —

```yaml
debounce_seconds: soon
max_customer_text_chars: lots
draft_ttl_hours: [24]
```

— raises out of plugin registration *before any handler is wired*. Business Mode then silently has no handlers at all (no connection updates, no owner DM capture, no `/biz`), and the traceback surfaces as a generic plugin-load failure that names no setting.

`_plugin_config()` is already documented as best-effort and swallows its own read errors; the coercion path should match that.

## Fix

- `_as_float(value, default)` / `_as_int(value, default)` helpers next to `register()`.
- The four call sites use them, so a junk value falls back to its default (8.0 s debounce, 24 h TTL, 4000 chars) instead of aborting registration. Valid values pass through unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/test_plugin_config.py`:

- direct helper behaviour for junk, `None`, list values;
- `register()` with every value junk: no raise, the wiring callback is registered and installs handlers;
- a valid `debounce_seconds: '3'` still reaches the manager as `3.0` (default stays 8.0 only for junk).

Both register-path tests fail before the change (`ValueError`).

## Also: the config was silently never read without PyYAML

CI installs core (`ruamel.yaml`) and caught this: `_plugin_config` did a bare `import yaml`. On any install without PyYAML that ImportError lands in the defensive `except` and every configured value becomes its default � quietly. The loader now tries core's `hermes_yaml` first (always present where a plugin runs, and what `hermes_cli.config` itself uses) with PyYAML only as the bare-checkout fallback, and the file is read as `utf-8`.

title: fix(business): collided debounce cleanup no longer drops the live timer
body:
## Problem

`handle_business_message` supersedes the per-`(connection, chat)` debounce timer on every new customer message: it pops the slot, cancels the prior task, and installs a replacement.

When the superseded timer is **already inside its draft call** (the LLM takes seconds, far longer than the debounce window), the replacement is in the slot by the time the old task's cleanup runs — and the cleanup popped the key unconditionally:

```python
finally:
    self._debounce_tasks.pop(key, None)   # pops the NEW task's handle
```

After that, later messages find `None`, cancel nothing, and the slot points at a dead task. Two timers can then arm for one burst, and the second one fires with an already-consumed buffer.

Cancellation itself is unaffected (the `except CancelledError: return` path exits before the cleanup block entirely — this was only ever about the slot handle).

## Fix

Keep the running task and only pop when the slot still holds it:

```python
task = asyncio.current_task()
...
finally:
    if self._debounce_tasks.get(key) is task:
        self._debounce_tasks.pop(key, None)
```

## Test

`test_superseded_timer_keeps_the_new_slot_handle` blocks the first draft call on an event, sends a second message while it is blocked (superseding the timer mid-run), then asserts the slot still holds a task. Fails before the change, passes after; the burst still yields exactly one owner DM carrying the latest text.

title: fix(record): listing survives a file deleted between glob and sort
body:
## Problem

`list_recordings` sorts entries with `p.stat().st_mtime` as the key, outside the per-file `try` that handles unreadable entries:

```python
for path in sorted(rec_dir.glob("*.json"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True):
```

Glob returning a path is not a promise the file still exists — a concurrent prune, a cleanup script, or the user deleting the folder contents between the glob and the sort makes `stat()` raise `FileNotFoundError` straight out of `hermes record --list`, so the rest of the recordings (including intact ones) are never listed.

## Fix

`_mtime(path)` helper: returns the mtime, or `0.0` when `stat()` fails. The loop's existing per-entry `except OSError` already turns the vanished file into an `unreadable` entry.

## Test

`test_file_removed_during_listing_does_not_crash` feeds one real file and one nonexistent path through a patched `Path.glob`:

- pre-change: `FileNotFoundError` propagates,
- post-change: both entries list, the real one with its step count, the vanished one marked `unreadable`.

title: fix(inbox): a host without psutil still renders the snapshot
body:
## Problem

`pid_alive` imports `psutil` at call time and nothing catches the import failing. `psutil` is not declared by this plugin, and both `collect_processes` and `collect_sessions` call straight into it — on a host without `psutil`, `hermes inbox` died with `ModuleNotFoundError` instead of rendering anything, taking the unrelated sections (cron, delegations, kanban) down with it. `hermes inbox` is advertised as a read-only snapshot; a missing optional dependency should degrade one probe, not the command.

## Fix

```python
try:
    import psutil
except ImportError:
    # Optional dependency: an unprobeable host PID is reported alive rather than
    # GONE, so a psutil-less environment shows the entries instead of flagging
    # every one of them as an orphan.
    return True
```

`True` (not `False`) keeps the semantic honest: the snapshot cannot prove the process is gone, and `False` would flood "Needs attention" with every entry.

## Test

`test_missing_psutil_does_not_crash_the_command` blocks the module (`sys.modules["psutil"] = None`) and asserts the collector still returns the entry with `alive: True`. Fails before the change with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

title: fix(business): stacking Edits keeps every captured draft
body:
## Problem

`_edit_capture` was `owner_chat_id -> draft_id`. When two drafts are waiting (two different customers) and the owner taps **Edit** on both — a normal thing to do while triaging — the second tap overwrote the first entry. The first draft's row stayed `pending` with no capture left: the owner's next message went to the *other* customer, and a second message could not deliver the first draft at all (the capture stack was empty, so it fell through to the normal text pipeline).

## Fix

A per-chat LIFO stack (`owner_chat_id -> [draft_id, …]`, newest last):

- Edit pushes its draft,
- a captured reply pops the newest one and delivers it,
- an empty attempt pushes its draft back (retry still works),
- the key is dropped when the stack empties.

Deliberately LIFO: the reply arrives immediately after a tap, so the newest Edit is the one the message belongs to.

## Test

`test_two_pending_edits_are_delivered_newest_first` arms two drafts on two customer chats, taps Edit on both, then sends two replies:

- each reply lands on its own customer chat (newest first),
- the third message is not consumed,
- both drafts end `edited`.

Fails before the change at the first delivery assertion (first reply goes to the wrong customer, second is never consumed).

title: fix(business): resolve the home through the host instead of HERMES_HOME only
body:
## Problem

Core resolves the Hermes home as context-local override → `HERMES_HOME` → platform default (`hermes_constants.get_hermes_home`, see the profile-fallback warning at `hermes_constants.py:188`). The plugin re-implemented only the env half:

```python
def _hermes_home() -> Path:
    home = os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME")
```

When the home is delivered through the context override — the documented path for a profile switch in a core subprocess — the environment is unset, so the plugin silently fell back to `~/.hermes`. `telegram-business/state.db` and the `config.yaml` read then target the **default profile**: connections and drafts land in the wrong profile and the user's configured settings are not the ones read.

## Fix

`_hermes_home()` asks `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` first and keeps the env/`~/.hermes` fallback for the bare-pytest case where core is not importable.

## Tests

`tests/test_home_resolution.py`:

- the override wins when core is importable (fails before the change),
- `HERMES_HOME` is honored when `hermes_constants` cannot be imported,
- the platform default is the last resort.

title: fix(record): escape attribute values in recorded selectors
body:
## Problem

`cssPath` builds attribute-hook selectors by interpolating raw values:

```js
else if (name) part += `[name="${name}"]`;
```

The id branch is safe via `CSS.escape()`, but the hooks it falls back to are not escaped. A field named `q"uote` (or a `data-testid` / `aria-label` containing a quote or backslash) records `input[name="q"uote"]` — an invalid selector that matches nothing, so the replay step for that field never finds its element. The whole point of the attribute hook is stability; a quoting bug defeats it.

## Fix

`cssAttr(v)` escapes `\` first, then `"`, and all three attribute hooks go through it. The `id` path keeps `CSS.escape()`.

## Tests

Both fail before the change:

- `test_quotes_and_backslashes_are_escaped` extracts the helper and evaluates it with `node` (skipped when node is unavailable) — `He said "hi" \ 100%` must come out as `He said \"hi\" \\ 100%`;
- `test_every_attribute_hook_goes_through_the_helper` asserts no raw `"${name}"`/`"${testId}"`/`"${aria}"` interpolation remains.

title: fix(business): expiry records the settlement time, not the cut-off
body:
## Problem

`expire_telegram_business_drafts` uses one value for both the `WHERE expires_at < ?` comparison and the `SET updated_at = ?` column:

```python
cutoff = now if now is not None else time.time()
... SET status = 'expired', updated_at = ? WHERE status = 'pending' AND expires_at < ?", (cutoff, cutoff)
```

`expires_at` is a deadline and comparing against the cut-off is right, but `updated_at` means "when this row was settled". A caller sweeping with a future cut-off (a catch-up sweep, tests stepping time, a clock skew) stamps rows into the future: `updated_at` can sit later than rows genuinely resolved in the normal flow, so any "most recent first" ordering built on it is wrong.

## Fix

The comparison keeps `cutoff`; `updated_at` takes `time.time()`.

## Test

`test_expire_stamps_updated_at_with_the_wall_clock` expires with `now = wall + 1 h` and asserts `before <= updated_at < cut_off`. Pre-change the row carries the cut-off and the assertion fails.

title: fix(record): cap the raw event buffer and keep the newest steps
body:
## Problem

The raw event buffer is a plain list that only gets read at save time (`build_recording` after Ctrl-C). Nothing bounded it, so a long demonstration — or a page that fires `change` on scroll — grew memory for the whole session. The recording is normalized at the end, so nothing on the hot path needs the earliest events.

## Fix

`MAX_RAW_EVENTS = 10_000` and a `_buffer_event` helper used by both append paths (recorder binding and top-frame navigation). Over the cap the oldest entry is dropped, keeping the tail: what the user just did is what must survive into the saved recording.

## Test

`test_buffer_keeps_the_newest_events_only` pushes `MAX + 3` payloads and asserts the buffer is exactly `MAX` long, starts at event 3 and ends at the newest one. Pre-change the buffer holds all `MAX + 3` (and the module has no constant, so the import fails).

`expire_telegram_business_drafts` uses one value for both the `WHERE expires_at < ?` comparison and the `SET updated_at = ?` column:

```python
cutoff = now if now is not None else time.time()
... SET status = 'expired', updated_at = ? WHERE status = 'pending' AND expires_at < ?", (cutoff, cutoff)
```

`expires_at` is a deadline and comparing against the cut-off is right, but `updated_at` means "when this row was settled". A caller sweeping with a future cut-off (a catch-up sweep, tests stepping time, a clock skew) stamps rows into the future: `updated_at` can sit later than rows genuinely resolved in the normal flow, so any "most recent first" ordering built on it is wrong.

## Fix

The comparison keeps `cutoff`; `updated_at` takes `time.time()`.

## Test

`test_expire_stamps_updated_at_with_the_wall_clock` expires with `now = wall + 1 h` and asserts `before <= updated_at < cut_off`. Pre-change the row carries the cut-off and the assertion fails.

title: fix(record): cap the raw event buffer and keep the newest steps
body:
## Problem

The raw event buffer is a plain list that only gets read at save time (`build_recording` after Ctrl-C). Nothing bounded it, so a long demonstration — or a page that fires `change` on scroll — grew memory for the whole session. The recording is normalized at the end, so nothing on the hot path needs the earliest events.

## Fix

`MAX_RAW_EVENTS = 10_000` and a `_buffer_event` helper used by both append paths (recorder binding and top-frame navigation). Over the cap the oldest entry is dropped, keeping the tail: what the user just did is what must survive into the saved recording.

## Test

`test_buffer_keeps_the_newest_events_only` pushes `MAX + 3` payloads and asserts the buffer is exactly `MAX` long, starts at event 3 and ends at the newest one. Pre-change the buffer holds all `MAX + 3` (and the module has no constant, so the import fails).

title: bug: fmt_age renders a boolean duration as seconds
body:
``fmt_age`` (inbox/report.py:70) gates only on ``isinstance(seconds, (int, float))``; ``bool`` passes, so ``fmt_age(True) == 1s``. A JSON duration that is a flag (``true``) shows a plausible but wrong age instead of the ``?`` used for non-durations.

Repro: ``fmt_age(True)`` -> 1s; expected ?.

title: bug: inbox process check ignores the recorded start time, so a recycled PID reads as alive
body:
`collect_processes` calls `pid_alive(entry.get("pid"))` (collectors.py:90) while `collect_sessions` passes the lease's `process_start_time` (collectors.py:217). `pid_alive`'s docstring promises a recycled PID is caught through the recorded start time, so the process section is the one place that guard never runs.

Effect: an orphaned checkpoint entry whose PID the OS reused renders as `running` in `hermes inbox` and is counted under "In progress" instead of "GONE (stale checkpoint)".

Repro: seed `processes.json` with the current PID and a clearly wrong `process_start_time`; the section still says running.

title: bug: Scheduled header prints for jobs with no next run, listing nothing
body:
`render_inbox` counts `active` before filtering out jobs without `next_run_at` (report.py:155-161):

```python
active = [j for j in ... if j.get("enabled") and not j.get("paused")]
...
upcoming = sorted((j for j in active if j.get("next_run_at")), ...)
lines.append(f"  ◆ Scheduled ({len(active)} active job(s))")
```

A job that is enabled but has no upcoming run (never scheduled, one-shot finished) still bumps the header count; with no job carrying `next_run_at` the header renders with zero lines under it.

Expected: count and list agree — count the jobs that will actually be listed.

title: bug: CDP endpoint discovery drops the query string of ws:// URLs
body:
`discovery_url` (workflow-record/cdp.py:56-64) rebuilds a bare `ws://host:port` URL as `http://host:port/json/version` and keeps nothing else:

```python
parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(value)
if parts.path not in ("", "/"):
    return None
scheme = "http" if low.startswith("ws://") else "https"
value = f"{scheme}://{parts.netloc}"
```

A `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/?token=abc` endpoint (common in front of remote CDP relays) loses `?token=abc`, so discovery calls `/json/version` unauthenticated and Hermes reports "no browser answered" even though the endpoint is reachable.

Expected: carry `parts.query` into the rebuilt URL.

title: ux: /biz off accepts any word as a chat id
body:
`handle_biz_command` stores `args[1]` verbatim in `paused_chats` (manager.py, `off`/`on` branches). Telegram chat ids are integers, but nothing validates the argument, so `/biz off @acme` answers "✓ Chat @acme muted in 1 connection(s)" and never matches a real chat — the owner gets a success confirmation for a mute with no effect.

Expected: reject a non-integer argument with the usage text so the mistake is visible at once.

title: fix(inbox): process entries honour their recorded start time
body:
Fixes #24

## Problem

`collect_processes` called `pid_alive(entry.get("pid"))` — the pid alone — while `collect_sessions` passes the lease's `process_start_time`. `pid_alive`'s contract is that a recycled PID is caught through the recorded start time, so the process section was the one caller the guard never covered: a stale checkpoint whose PID the OS has since reused displayed as `running` and was counted under "In progress" instead of "GONE (stale checkpoint)".

## Fix

Pass `entry.get("process_start_time")`, like the session collector.

## Test

`test_recycled_pid_is_detected_through_the_start_time` seeds the current PID twice: once with the real start time, once with a start time 5000 s off. Only the first may read alive. Fails before the change.

title: fix(inbox): Scheduled header counts only jobs that are listed
body:
Fixes #25

## Problem

`render_inbox` computed the header count before filtering out jobs that have no upcoming run (report.py:155-161), so an enabled one-shot or never-scheduled job inflated `Scheduled (N active job(s))`, and with no job carrying `next_run_at` the header printed with zero lines under it.

## Fix

Filter first (`scheduled`), then print the header with `len(scheduled)` and list the first five. An empty set leaves the section out entirely.

## Tests

- `test_scheduled_header_matches_the_jobs_listed`: one job with `next_run_at` plus one without → count 1, unscheduled job absent from the section; only the unscheduled job → no section at all (fails before the change).
- the existing section-render test's expectation moves from `(2 active job(s))` to `(1 active job(s))`, which is the point of the fix.

title: fix(record): keep the query when discovering a CDP endpoint
body:
Fixes #26

## Problem

`discovery_url` rebuilt a bare `ws://host:port` endpoint as `http://host:port/json/version` and threw the rest of the URL away — including its query:

```python
parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(value)
...
value = f"{scheme}://{parts.netloc}"
```

CDP relays (and any tunnel put in front of a browser) commonly hand out `ws://host:port/?token=…`. Discovery then requests `/json/version` unauthenticated, gets refused, and `hermes record` reports "no browser answered at …" for a reachable endpoint. The `http` branch had the same shape of bug: a query was appended after the string that already ended in a path, producing `…?token=x/json/version`.

## Fix

The ws branch returns the version URL with the query preserved after the path; the http branch splits the query off before appending `/json/version` and reattaches it.

## Test

Two new parametrized cases in `test_discovery_url` (`ws://…/?token=abc`, `wss://…?token=abc`) assert the rebuilt URL keeps the query at the end. Both fail before the change.

title: fix(business): reject a non-numeric /biz off chat id
body:
Fixes #27

## Problem

`handle_biz_command` takes `args[1]` verbatim as a chat id. Nothing checks it, so `/biz off @acme` answers `✓ Chat @acme muted in 1 connection(s)` — a success confirmation for a value no customer chat will ever equal. The mistake is invisible; the owner thinks the chat is muted and keeps getting drafts for it.

## Fix

Before writing, require the argument to be an integer (optional leading `-`, for group ids) and otherwise answer with a short hint pointing at the numeric id plus the two relevant usage lines.

## Tests

- `test_off_rejects_a_non_numeric_chat_id` (`@acme`, `carol`, `12x`): reply says it isn't a chat id, `paused_chats` stays empty — fails before the change;
- `test_off_accepts_a_negative_group_id`: `-100123` is still stored.

title: fix(inbox): a boolean duration renders as unknown, not 1s
body:
Fixes #23

## Problem

`fmt_age` gates only on `isinstance(seconds, (int, float))`, and `bool` is an `int` subclass — a duration arriving as a JSON flag (`true`) renders as a plausible `1s` instead of the `?` the function uses for anything that is not a real duration.

## Fix

Exclude `bool` explicitly.

## Test

`TestFmtAge` — `True`/`False` render `?` (fails before the change), real numbers keep formatting as before.

title: inbox: add /inbox slash command via ctx.register_command
body:
Adds an `/inbox` slash command to the inbox plugin, using the documented
`ctx.register_command` plugin API (developer guide -> Register slash commands),
so the same read-only report is reachable from any chat surface where the
plugin is enabled - not just the `hermes inbox` CLI subcommand.

- The handler returns the existing report (`render_inbox(build_inbox())`) as
  plain text; long reports are truncated just under 4096 chars for messaging
  surfaces.
- Read-only: no tools, no hooks, nothing runs during normal chats. The CLI
  subcommand is untouched.
- The command auto-appears in /help (and platform command menus) per the
  plugin API - no extra wiring.

Tests: extends the existing PluginManager-based registration tests - the slash
command registers only when the plugin is enabled, the handler returns the
seeded report under the 4096-char cap, and an oversized report comes back
truncated under it. Full plugin suite passes (32 tests).

title: feat: github-copilot model-provider plugin (copilot + copilot-acp), moved out of core
body:
Adds `github-copilot`: GitHub Copilot as a Hermes model provider, moved out of hermes-agent core. One plugin registers both providers: `copilot` (the Copilot API with your GitHub account) and `copilot-acp` (your installed Copilot CLI over ACP).

**Requires the core change in NousResearch/hermes-agent#144788** (branch `copilot-seams/integration`). That PR takes Copilot out of core and adds the generic `ProviderProfile` seams these profiles fill. This repo's CI checks out hermes-agent `main`, which still bundles Copilot, so until #144788 merges:
- the plugin suite runs only the inert-guard tests (1 passed, 3 skipped); the modules that need the seams are not collected;
- `plugins validate` fails at the capability probe ("registered no ProviderProfile"). That's expected: the plugin stays inert on a core that still serves Copilot.

Once #144788 merges, re-run `tests.yml` before merging this PR. No `requires_hermes` yet, because no release has the seams.

## What's in it
- **Code:** the in-tree `plugins/model-providers/copilot` and `copilot-acp` at integration `10312d0c9ce`, imported verbatim first. The first commit lists the source paths. Only the sibling import changed: `copilot_acp` now reaches `copilot` by relative import.
- **Inert on old cores:** registers nothing and logs one warning if the running core either still ships `plugins/model-providers/copilot{,-acp}/__init__.py` (resolved from the imported `providers` module, the same way core's discovery finds it), or lacks the seams. That way nothing gets registered twice and the core's own Copilot is never shadowed.
- **Catalog rule 11, partial cut (maintainer ruling):**
  - **Kept:** the GitHub→Copilot token exchange (editor OAuth client id), device-code login, and the env tokens `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`, now read through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`.
  - **Removed:**
    - the `gh auth token` fallback and its cache;
    - the `gh_cli` pool source and its removal step;
    - reads of `~/.copilot/config.json` and `~/.config/github-copilot/{hosts,apps}.json` (sign-in evidence and catalog token);
    - `catalog_credential_files`.
  - A `gh_cli` row the old core had pooled gets pruned on the next pool load (checked against the integration core).
- **`hermes auth add copilot`** now runs the GitHub device-code sign-in through `auth_handler` and pools the token. `--api-key`, other actions, and runs without a terminal keep core's built-in path. This replaces `gh auth login` in every message.

## Tests (against hermes-agent `copilot-seams/integration`: `1da2eb42dc6` is the removal commit, `129f205a0e8` the current head)
| Core | Plugin suite | `plugins validate` | Install scanner |
|---|---|---|---|
| integration `129f205a0e8` (Copilot removed) | 144 passed | passed, 0 private-import warnings | `safe` |
| hermes-agent `main` `0107da5d2a3` (still bundles Copilot, no seams) | 1 passed, 3 skipped (inert) | fails by design (no profile) | `safe` |
| v0.22.5 (latest stable) scanner | — | — | `safe` |

Earlier heads were tested on integration `129f205a0e8` (138 passed at `03d140d`), `53a51a49cc1` (135 passed) and `1da2eb42dc6` (121 passed). Those cores still have `process_command_fallback` and lack the public names below, so this head needs `129f205a0e8` or later.

- **Ported tests:** the 12 core Copilot test files. Only import paths changed, except the gh-only cases:
  - deleted: classic PAT from `gh` raises, and the gh probe cache;
  - the two "invalid env var skips gh" cases keep their empty-result assertions and now prove no subprocess is spawned.
- **New tests:**
  - real discovery from a `HERMES_HOME/plugins/github-copilot` install (both names and aliases resolve, source `user`);
  - both inert guards;
  - a leftover `__pycache__`-only dir doesn't count as bundled;
  - rule 11: every old token store plus a `gh` on PATH, an audit hook proves none is opened or run. This test is red on the pre-cut commit;
  - `hermes auth add copilot` driven through core's real `auth_add_command`.
- **Private core imports: 32 sites / 21 symbols → 0.** Self-contained helpers are vendored in `copilot/helpers.py` (host matching, the effort-ladder clamp, the catalog JSON GET, prompts). The rest moved to documented surfaces: `agent.credential_pool`, `auth_model_picker.prompt_model_selection`, `resolve_external_process_provider_credentials`, the profile's own fields, and the public names #144788 added for the last three: `hermes_cli.model_setup.persist_model_selection` (was `model_setup_flows_common._persist_model`), `hermes_cli.model_setup.note_setup_failure` (was `_note_setup_failure`) and `agent.secret_scope.secret_source_label` (was `env_loader.format_secret_source_suffix`). They are used directly: every core with the seams has them.
- **The plugin only calls GitHub for a home that chose Copilot** (`copilot/activation.py`). Before, with `GH_TOKEN` in `.env` and another provider configured, `hermes status` exchanged that token at api.github.com and fetched Copilot `/models`. Cause: status lists the providers it can authenticate, the listing warms each provider's model cache on a background thread (`cached_provider_model_ids` → `provider_model_ids`), and that reached this plugin's `picker_catalog`, whose token lookup ran the exchange. The model pickers, Desktop model options and pool loads took the same path (core's `explicitly_configured()` counts `GH_TOKEN`, because it's one of the profile's env vars). Now "chose Copilot" means one of: `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set; `copilot` is named in `config.yaml` (`model`, fallback, `delegation`, an `auxiliary` task, MoA); there's a `hermes auth add copilot` pool row; or you're in `hermes model` → Copilot / Copilot ACP. Otherwise the picker shows the curated list and the token stays raw. `GH_TOKEN` still counts as a credential once you've chosen Copilot.
  - Unit test: `tests/test_activation_gate.py` drives core's real `provider_model_ids`, `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials` and `load_pool`. It fails on `7a83444`, passes here, and checks each configured state positively.
  - Live stand-in (`hermes status`, s8): base sent an exchange plus a `/models` call. This head sends 0 GitHub requests.
- **`x-initiator` as in Hermes core (premium requests).** By design, `copilot` sends `x-initiator: agent` on every request, except the first request of a user turn on the exact host `api.githubcopilot.com` (and GitHub Models, `models.github.ai`), which says `user`: the hosts core's `_is_copilot_url` matched. Plan hosts from the token exchange (`api.individual.` / `api.business.` / `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`) send `agent` on every request, as on core. An earlier head of this PR widened the hook to the whole host family; `1d317ec` restores core's set. The README's "Premium requests" section states this.
  - The `/models` validation probe keeps its security fix: it used a URL-prefix test that missed every plan host and accepted `https://api.githubcopilot.com.evil.test`; it now matches by hostname over the Copilot host family. The token still only ever goes to the constant `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models`.
  - Unit tests (`tests/test_copilot_hosts.py`): the profile hook and core's `route_answer` (for `copilot` and a `custom` route) give `user` on `api.githubcopilot.com` and nothing on plan hosts or lookalikes; a real offline `AIAgent.chat` turn (stand-in HTTP transport) sends `user` on `api.githubcopilot.com` and `agent` on `api.individual.githubcopilot.com`. 8 tests are red on `03d140d`.
  - Live stand-in (s1–s10 harness, base `0c771d7a5ba` vs core `129f205a0e8` + this plugin at `623a2f6`, whose code differs from this head only in comments, docstrings and README): main requests byte-identical to base in s1–s7 and s10, including `x-initiator` (every main and auxiliary request says `agent` on both arms; the stand-in serves `api.individual.githubcopilot.com`). Remaining deltas are the documented ones: s1 config block / picker output, s3 and s8 catalog + exchange gating (no GitHub calls until Copilot is chosen), s8 `hermes status` provider label (`GitHub Copilot` instead of `github-copilot`, from #144788's picker label), s9 the rule-11 cut (a `gh auth token`-only home no longer authenticates; it now ends with ``No usable credentials found for provider 'copilot'. Set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN. Run `hermes auth add copilot` to sign in.``), s10 stdout/system prompt. s7 (ACP) identical.
- **Sign-in hints on missing-credential errors**, through two seams #144788 added:
  - `missing_credentials_hint`: with no credential, runtime resolution says ``No usable credentials found for provider 'copilot'. Set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN. Run `hermes auth add copilot` to sign in.`` CLI and Desktop readiness say ``No usable credentials found for copilot. Run `hermes auth add copilot` to sign in.`` The hook gets no caller context, so one string serves both; it no longer repeats `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` after core's own list. A `gh auth login` alone no longer signs Hermes in, so those users used to hit a bare error.
  - `auth_required_hint`: when the Copilot CLI answers with ACP's auth-required error, the message gets ``Run `copilot login` to sign in to the GitHub Copilot CLI.`` (`copilot login` is from GitHub's Copilot CLI command reference.)
  - Tests (`tests/test_missing_credentials_hints.py`) drive core's real `resolve_runtime_provider`, `check_runtime_readiness` and a signed-out stand-in CLI. All 3 fail without the hints.
- **`process_command_fallback` dropped:** #144788 removed that field (a pinned `delegation.command` that no profile names now keeps the selected provider). On `129f205a0e8`, passing it failed the plugin's import with a `TypeError`. The six main-agent reasoning clamp cases no longer call core's private `_endpoint_reasoning_payload`: they run a real `AIAgent.chat` turn through a stand-in HTTP transport (`conftest.offline_chat_turn`) and assert the request body's `reasoning` field. Assertions unchanged; a pass-through clamp turns them red.
- **Fixes on hermes-agent `main` since the seams base `0c771d7a5ba`:** none touch Copilot (`git log -S copilot 0c771d7a5ba..5b32cfc2300` was empty when checked), so nothing needed porting.
- **CI on this repo:** `tests.yml` checks out hermes-agent `main`, which has no seams. There, the test modules that build the profiles used to error at collection (7 errors). They're now skipped on an inert core; the inert-guard tests still run. `plugins validate` on `main` also lists `hermes_cli.model_setup.*`, `agent.acp_client.ACPClient` and `resolve_external_process_provider_credentials` as private imports: `main` doesn't have those modules and names yet. The lint in #144788 knows them, and `129f205a0e8` reports 0.

Not merging: this lands after #144788.






## Infographic

![copilot-leaves-core](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe04b/J9YTA6KPUjO7u0fywvibT_mRC3uiyl.png)

title: github-copilot: decide whether to send x-initiator: user on the first call of each turn (premium requests)
body:
Decision needed: should Hermes mark the first request of each user turn `x-initiator: user` on GitHub Copilot?

**What happens today:** Copilot counts a premium request when a request carries `x-initiator: user`; requests marked `agent` don't count. Hermes intends to send `user` on the first model call of each user turn and `agent` on tool-loop follow-ups (like VS Code). But the check only matched the exact host `api.githubcopilot.com`, while real accounts are routed by the token exchange to `api.individual.githubcopilot.com`, `api.business.githubcopilot.com` or `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`. On those hosts the header was never set, so every request went out with the client default `agent`. Net effect: Copilot users have been billed almost no premium requests through Hermes.

This behaviour shipped in Hermes core for months and was kept unchanged when Copilot moved into this plugin (Teknium ruling: keep billing behaviour identical in the move, decide the fix separately).

**Options**
- A, keep as is: users keep today's premium-request consumption. Risk: Hermes under-reports user-initiated requests to GitHub compared with first-party clients.
- B, fix the host match: one premium request per user turn (VS Code parity). Users' premium usage rises noticeably; needs a release-note callout.

Evidence: local stand-in run of real `hermes chat` sessions showing `x-initiator: agent` on the first call of every user turn on `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` (hermes-agent#144788 campaign notes); the one-line fix lives in `github-copilot/copilot/wire.py` (`request_headers` host set).

title: [Feature]: Add a GitHub Copilot fetcher to /usage account limits
body:
## Feature Description

Add a `copilot` entry to `_USAGE_FETCHERS` in `agent/account_usage.py` so the `/usage` account-limits block shows GitHub Copilot quota alongside Codex, Anthropic and OpenRouter.

## Motivation

Users on GitHub Copilot (including the Copilot Free plan) have no visibility into their remaining quota from Hermes. Copilot Free has hard monthly caps (chat + completions), and when exhausted, requests fail until the monthly reset. Every other provider with a fetcher surfaces this in `/usage`; Copilot — a first-class provider in the picker — silently shows nothing.

GitHub exposes this data on an endpoint the provider's own token can already read:

- `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` with `Authorization: token <COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN>` returns `quota_snapshots` with per-quota `remaining`, `percent_remaining` and `credits_used` (quotas observed: `chat`, `completions`, `premium_interactions`), plus `quota_reset_date` and `access_type_sku` (e.g. `free_limited_copilot`).
- The token is the same `gho_*` OAuth token the provider already stores (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / credential pool), so no new auth or scopes are needed.

## Proposed Solution

Add `_fetch_copilot_account_usage` and register it:

```python
_USAGE_FETCHERS = {
    "openai-codex": _fetch_codex_account_usage,
    "anthropic": _fetch_anthropic_account_usage,
    "openrouter": _fetch_openrouter_account_usage,
    "copilot": _fetch_copilot_account_usage,
}
```

The fetcher resolves the raw token via `hermes_cli.copilot_auth.resolve_copilot_token()`, calls the endpoint above (it must use `Authorization: token <gho_*>` on the raw GitHub token, **not** the exchanged Copilot API JWT — the JWT endpoint paths differ), maps each `quota_snapshots` entry to an `AccountUsageWindow` (used/total/percent + reset date), and returns an `AccountUsageSnapshot` via the existing `_snapshot()` helper. Note `premium_interactions` has `has_quota: false` on the free plan and should be skipped or rendered accordingly.

Example `/usage` output for a free-plan account: chat 200/200, completions 2000/2000, resets 2026-10-01.

## Alternatives Considered

- Leaving it to users to check github.com/settings/copilot — easy to miss, and quota exhaustion fails turns with a confusing error.
- A plugin — this belongs in the same table as the existing three fetchers; a plugin cannot render into `/usage`'s account-limits block.

## Scope / Effort Estimate

Small — one fetcher function (~20 lines) + one table entry in `agent/account_usage.py`; no new dependencies, no schema changes. Possibly worth a small invariant test following the pattern of the other fetchers.

## Additional Context

Verified live against the API on 2026-09-19 with a Copilot Free account (token exchange + `quota_snapshots` both returned as described). Related: NousResearch/hermes-agent#36276 (quota-exhaustion retry behaviour) and NousResearch/hermes-agent#29442 (copilot credential detection).

title: Copilot: grok-4.5 routed to /chat/completions -> HTTP 400; responses-only model needs Responses API
body:
## Summary
Selecting `grok-4.5` on the GitHub Copilot provider fails with:
```
HTTP 400: model "grok-4.5" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint
```

## Root cause
GitHub Copilot only serves `grok-4.5` via the **Responses API** — the live model catalog advertises `grok-4.5 -> ['/responses']`. But Hermes' Copilot API-mode routing only routes **GPT-5+** models to the Responses API.

`hermes_cli/models.py::_should_use_copilot_responses_api` returns `True` only for `gpt-5+` (excluding `gpt-5-mini`). Its docstring explicitly hardcodes *"All non-GPT models (Claude, Gemini, etc.) use Chat Completions."* So `grok-4.5` falls through to `chat_completions` and the API rejects it.

Verified against the live catalog (`GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models`):
| model | supported_endpoints |
|---|---|
| `grok-4.5` | `['/responses']` (only) |
| `gpt-5.4` | `['/responses','/chat/completions','ws:/responses']` |
| `gpt-5-mini` | `['/chat/completions','/responses','ws:/responses']` |
| `claude-sonnet-5` | `['/v1/messages','/chat/completions']` |
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | `['/chat/completions']` |

Only `grok-4.5` (and any future `/responses`-only non-GPT family) hits this bug.

## Repro
```
hermes -m grok-4.5 --provider copilot -z "reply with exactly: OK"
# GIVES: HTTP 400: model "grok-4.5" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint
```

## Fix (local patch in this checkout)
1. `_should_use_copilot_responses_api`: also return `True` for `grok*` / `x-ai/grok*` model IDs.
2. `copilot_model_api_mode`: after the GPT-5 pattern check, consult the catalog's `supported_endpoints` — if `/responses` is present and `/chat/completions` is absent, return `codex_responses`. This is future-proof for any non-GPT `/responses`-only model, not just grok.

## Verification
- Functional: `grok-4.5` -> `should_responses=True`, `api_mode=codex_responses`; `gpt-5.4` / `gpt-5-mini` / `claude` / `gemini` unchanged.
- E2E: `hermes -m grok-4.5 --provider copilot -z "reply with exactly: OK"` -> `OK`.

## Suggest
Rather than hardcode the grok family, consider making `copilot_model_api_mode` use the live catalog's `supported_endpoints` as the authoritative signal (as the fix does) and mirror that in the auxiliary-client `_should_use_copilot_responses_api` hot path.

title: [Bug]: Copilot grok-4.6 fails with HTTP 400 (not accessible via /chat/completions)
body:
# GitHub Copilot grok-4.6 fails with HTTP 400 ("not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint")

### Description

Setting the default model to `grok-4.6` on the GitHub Copilot provider fails on the first request. Streaming never starts, and no assistant output is delivered.

The same model/provider combination starts working after `model.api_mode` is set to `codex_responses`.

This was reproduced on current `main` after a gateway restart, including Discord.

Related open report for the same Copilot HTTP 400 on `grok-4.5`: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins/issues/37

### Environment

- **Hermes Version**: `v0.20.6 (2026.8.27) · upstream 99c3cad8`
- **OS**: Linux x86_64 (WSL2)
- **Model**: `grok-4.6` (via GitHub Copilot)
- **Python**: 3.11.15

### Reproduction Steps

1. Set the default model to `grok-4.6` with provider `copilot`. Leave `model.api_mode` unset.
2. Restart Hermes / the messaging gateway.
3. Send any message (CLI or Discord gateway).

### Expected Behavior

`grok-4.6` on GitHub Copilot completes the request and streams a reply.

### Actual Behavior

The request fails before any assistant output is delivered:

```text
2026-08-28 13:02:45,650 ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'model "grok-4.6" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint', 'code': 'unsupported_api_for_model'}}
```

Setting `model.api_mode: codex_responses` and restarting allowed `grok-4.6` on Copilot to work.

title: [Feature]: Support GitHub Copilot on GitHub Enterprise Server (GHE)
body:
### Problem or Use Case

 ## Summary

 The current Copilot provider only works with `github.com`. It does not support **GitHub Enterprise Server (GHE)** instances where the Copilot token endpoint and proxy
are hosted on a custom domain.

 ## Current Behavior

 When selecting "GitHub Copilot" via `hermes model`, the OAuth device code flow always redirects to `https://github.com/login/device`. The Copilot token endpoint is
hardcoded to `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`.

 For GHE Server users, this results in:
 - OAuth login pointing to the wrong host
 - Token exchange returning `401 Bad credentials` (because the GHE token is not valid on `api.github.com`)


### Proposed Solution

Add a config option `copilot.github_host` (default: `github.com`).

 Example config (`~/.hermes/config.yaml`):

     copilot:
       github_host: "ghe.example.com"

 Or via env var: `COPILOT_GITHUB_HOST=ghe.example.com`

 Changes needed:

 1. Auto-detect from `~/.config/github-copilot/apps.json` — if a GHE host entry exists, offer it during `hermes model` setup
 2. OAuth device flow should target `https://{github_host}/login/device` instead of hardcoded `https://github.com/login/device`
 3. Token endpoint should use `https://{github_host}/api/v3/copilot_internal/v2/token` instead of `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`
 4. Use the `endpoints` object from the token response dynamically (it returns `endpoints.proxy`, `endpoints.api`) instead of hardcoding github.com URLs

### Alternatives Considered

Tried using "Enter a token manually" with the GHE OAuth token, but Hermes still calls api.github.com for token exchange,
which rejects the GHE token with 401.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

title: [Bug]: Claude-on-Copilot silently drops configured reasoning_effort
body:
## What happened

A configured `reasoning_effort` (e.g. `high`) is silently dropped for every Claude-on-Copilot request (`api.githubcopilot.com` / `models.github.ai` routes). The request goes out with no reasoning effort applied, even though the live Copilot `/models` catalog advertises `capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort` for those models.

## Root cause

`AIAgent` has two reasoning gates that resolve supported effort levels:

- `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()`
- `_github_models_reasoning_extra_body()`

For the Copilot routes both call `github_model_reasoning_efforts(self.model)` with no catalog and no api_key. With no catalog it falls through to the static GPT/o-series table (`_github_reasoning_efforts_for_model_id`), which has no Claude entry and returns `[]`. Net result:

- `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()` -> `False`
- `_github_models_reasoning_extra_body()` -> `None`

So the configured effort is never sent.

## Reproduce

1. Configure a Copilot-hosted Claude model (opus or sonnet) with `reasoning_effort: high`.
2. Issue any request.
3. Observe the outbound request carries no reasoning_effort; the gates resolve to `False` / `None`.

Control: `github_model_reasoning_efforts(model_id)` with no catalog returns `[]` for Claude model ids.

## Expected

The gates should resolve supported efforts from the live Copilot `/models` catalog, which already advertises `reasoning_effort` support for these models, and apply the configured effort.

## Fix

PR NousResearch/hermes-agent#51953 resolves this by supplying the live `/models` catalog to `github_model_reasoning_efforts(...)` via a cached `get_copilot_reasoning_efforts(model_id, api_key)` wrapper, degrading gracefully to the static table when offline.

title: [Bug]: GHEC Copilot provider ignores enterprise token exchange / Copilot API host
body:
### Bug Description

Hermes supports `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`, but GitHub Enterprise Cloud Copilot still fails after updates because parts of the Copilot provider assume public GitHub endpoints.

Setup:
- Hermes v0.20.5
- `COPILOT_GH_HOST=<enterprise>.ghe.com`
- `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL=https://copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com`
- `model.provider=copilot`
- `model.base_url=https://copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com`

Observed:
- Hermes exchanges the `ghu_` token against `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`
- This returns HTTP 401 for GHEC tokens
- Some request paths only treat `*.githubcopilot.com` as Copilot API hosts, so GHEC hosts miss required Copilot headers like `Editor-Version`

Expected:
- If `COPILOT_GH_HOST` is set to `<enterprise>.ghe.com`, token exchange should try:
  - `https://api.<enterprise>.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`
  - optionally `https://<enterprise>.ghe.com/api/v3/copilot_internal/v2/token`
- `copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com` should be recognized as a Copilot API host for header injection.
- `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL` should be respected end-to-end.

Workaround:
A local patch adding GHEC exchange endpoint selection and recognizing `copilot-api.*.ghe.com` as a Copilot API host fixes the issue, but `hermes update` overwrites it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/update Hermes to current `main` / v0.20.5.
2. Authenticate GitHub Copilot against a GitHub Enterprise Cloud host:
   ```bash
   hermes model
   # Select GitHub Copilot
   # Complete OAuth/device login against <enterprise>.ghe.com
3. Configure the enterprise Copilot API endpoint:
    hermes config set COPILOT_GH_HOST <enterprise>.ghe.com
    hermes config set COPILOT_API_BASE_URL https://copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com
    hermes config set model.provider copilot
    hermes config set model.base_url https://copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com
    hermes config set model.default gpt-5.4
4. Run a minimal request:
    hermes --provider copilot --model gpt-5.4 --cli --safe-mode -z "Reply with exactly OK."

### Expected Behavior

When `COPILOT_GH_HOST=<enterprise>.ghe.com` is set, Hermes should exchange the token using the enterprise API host, for example: https://api.<enterprise>.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token
OR:
https://<enterprise>.ghe.com/api/v3/copilot_internal/v2/token

Then Hermes should use the returned endpoint:
https://copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com
and include the required Copilot headers for that host.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes fails with HTTP 401, and logs show it is still using public GitHub Copilot assumptions:

HTTP 401: unauthorized: AuthenticateToken authentication failed
Provider: copilot
Endpoint: https://api.githubcopilot.com

The token exchange attempts `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`, which rejects GHEC `ghu_` tokens.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_
