title: fix(github-copilot): serve fine-grained PATs under the Copilot CLI identity
body:
This PR is picking up earlier Issues in hermes-agent core, for making it possible to use Github PATs to access copilot. 
Disclaimer: The whole fix and following documentation is written with AI. Maybe this PR can be used or it can act as guidance for a fix, so this issue can be fixed and we get copilot working with a github PAT.

  A github_pat_ token is a valid Copilot bearer but the API rejects it with 400
  "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint" under the VS Code
  Editor-Version / Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat pair, and the exchange
  endpoint 404s for it. Requests carrying a fine-grained PAT now present the
  Copilot CLI attribution (copilot-developer-cli, copilot/<version>); exchanged
  gho_/ghu_ tokens keep the VS Code identity the exchange itself requires.

  The token is no longer sent to the exchange: get_copilot_api_token returns it
  as-is and the aux-401 / stale-credential refreshers hand it straight back, so
  the once-per-process "exchange degraded to RAW token" warning no longer fires
  for the documented PAT path. The catalog fetch threads its key into the header
  builder, so /models lists the account catalog with a PAT too (43 models
  instead of the 39 the vscode-chat id returns, verified live).

  Tests cover the attribution per token family on client_headers and headers,
  the image-turn path, no exchange attempt, and no degradation warning.

  Superseded for this path by the closed core PRs:
  - NousResearch/hermes-agent#51411 (identity consolidation, closed when Copilot left core)
  - NousResearch/hermes-agent#96191 (same closure, enterprise hosts) Both were closed with "a PR against hermes-labs-plugins is the place" — this is that PR.

title: github-copilot: Claude on /chat/completions ignores cache_ttl and hides cache writes; /v1/messages honors 1h caching
body:
## Problem

The github-copilot plugin routes every Claude model to Copilot's OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` (`copilot/wire.py`, `model_api_mode`: only GPT-5+ except gpt-5-mini go to `codex_responses`; everything else is `chat_completions`). On that route:

1. **`prompt_caching.cache_ttl` has no effect.** Hermes core's cache policy (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`, the Anthropic prompt-cache policy) returns `(False, False)` for provider copilot + `chat_completions` + Claude, so no `cache_control` markers are sent. Adding markers by hand doesn't help either: Copilot caches automatically, but the cache was gone after 7.5 minutes idle even with a 1h marker (consistent with a short fixed lifetime, likely 5 min; only a 7.5-min gap was tested).
2. **Cache writes are invisible.** The `/chat/completions` usage block only has `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`; there is no cache-write field, so Hermes records `cache_write_tokens = 0` and counts writes as ordinary input. If Copilot bills those writes at the cache-write rate (as it does on `/v1/messages`), Hermes under-reports cost.

Copilot's Anthropic-format endpoint `/v1/messages` (the one Claude Code uses) behaves differently: it honors `cache_control` with `ttl: "1h"` and reports `cache_creation_input_tokens`, split into `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`.

## Evidence (2026-10-29, Copilot usage-based billing)

Same ~37-45K-token prompt, re-sent after 7.5 minutes idle (`max_tokens: 5`):

| Endpoint | Model | Marker | Immediately | After 7.5 min idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/chat/completions` | claude-sonnet-5.5 | none | cached | **miss** |
| `/chat/completions` | claude-sonnet-5.5 | 5m (message-level `cache_control`) | cached | **miss** |
| `/chat/completions` | claude-sonnet-5.5 | 1h (message-level `cache_control`) | cached | **miss** |
| `/v1/messages` | claude-opus-5.5 | 1h | written (1h) | **hit** (38,026 read) |
| `/v1/messages` | claude-opus-5.5 | 5m | written (5m) | miss, rewritten |
| `/v1/messages` | claude-sonnet-5.5 | 1h | written (1h) | **hit** (45,532 read) |
| `/v1/messages` | claude-sonnet-5.5 | 5m | written (5m) | miss, rewritten |

Billing per 1M tokens, from the `copilot_usage.token_details` block that `/v1/messages` returns (`cost_per_batch` / 1e11 = USD per 1M tokens):

| Model | Input | Cache read | 5m write (`cache_write`) | 1h write (`cache_write_1h`) | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-opus-5.5 | $4.00 | $0.20 | $5.00 | $8.00 | $20.00 |
| claude-sonnet-5.5 | $2.00 | $0.10 | $2.50 | $4.00 | $10.00 |

Note: block-array system content on `/chat/completions` (`"content": [{"type": "text", ..., "cache_control": ...}]`) was silently dropped (prompt_tokens collapsed to just the user message), so block-level markers are not an option on that route.

## Impact

For human-paced chats (desktop/TUI) with 5-60 minute pauses, every pause forces a full-context rewrite at the 5m write rate. On one heavy user's history (Oct 1-29), a rough upper-bound model of a 1h cache for interactive sessions (`cache_ttl: auto`) gives a rough single-digit-percent reduction in Copilot spend (upper bound; the model treats all uncached input as writes, so it likely overstates).

## Proposal

Route Copilot Claude models to `anthropic_messages` (`/v1/messages`), with the Copilot auth contract: bearer token via the SDK's `auth_token` (not `x-api-key`), the Copilot editor/initiator/vision headers, and the `context-1m-2025-08-07` beta. This is the routing from NousResearch/hermes-agent#49184 (by @arminanton, which was about auth and 1M context, not caching), closed when Copilot moved into this plugin. With that route, core's existing `is_anthropic_wire and is_claude` branch applies native cache markers and `cache_ttl`.

Happy to send a PR (after verifying on `/v1/messages`: tool calls, streaming, reasoning effort, images, >200K context, x-initiator/premium accounting, and cache hits across a real multi-turn session) if the maintainers are open to moving Claude off the chat endpoint.

Related: #46 (long-context tiers hidden), #40 (Claude-on-Copilot drops reasoning_effort).

Env: hermes-agent v0.22.5+, github-copilot plugin (labs), macOS.

title: feat(github-copilot): route Claude to Copilot's /v1/messages for prompt-cache TTLs and cache-write usage
body:
## Summary

This routes GitHub Copilot's Claude models to Copilot's Anthropic-format `/v1/messages` endpoint (`api_mode: anthropic_messages`) instead of the OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`. The profile answers core's new `anthropic_auth_style` hook with `bearer` for `githubcopilot.com` hosts, and its existing `client_headers` supplies the Copilot editor headers. GPT-5+ (Responses) and every other model are unchanged.

**Requires two hermes-agent PRs:** NousResearch/hermes-agent#146877 adds the `ProviderProfile.anthropic_auth_style` seam, and NousResearch/hermes-agent#146876 scopes a saved `model.api_mode` to the saved default model. The route needs both: without the seam core sends the Copilot token as `x-api-key` (a 401), and without the fix a saved Claude wire would pin every other Copilot model. The plugin feature-detects each; on a core missing either, Claude stays on `chat_completions` as today (setup's no-saved-`api_mode` change is harmless there), so this PR is safe to merge before or after the core PRs.

Part of #56; with both core PRs merged, this fixes it.

## Why

On `/chat/completions`, Copilot's Claude loses most of the benefit of prompt caching:

- **TTLs are ignored.** With a ~37-43K-token prompt (`claude-sonnet-5.5`, direct API requests, not through Hermes), the cache hit immediately (36,525 of 36,536 tokens cached) but was gone after 7.5 minutes idle (0 cached), whether the request had no marker, a 5m marker, or a 1h marker.
- **Cache writes are hidden.** The usage block has only `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, so Hermes records `cache_write_tokens = 0`.

On `/v1/messages`, `cache_control` with `ttl: "1h"` is honored: the same 7.5-minute gap read 38,026 tokens (`claude-opus-5.5`) and 45,532 tokens (`claude-sonnet-5.5`) from cache, and usage reports cache writes (`cache_creation_input_tokens`, split into 5m and 1h under `cache_creation`). Core's Anthropic-wire Claude branch applies its cache markers and `prompt_caching.cache_ttl`, with no plugin code needed.

## What changed

- `github-copilot/copilot/wire.py`:
  - `core_serves_anthropic_bearer()` and `core_scopes_saved_api_mode()` feature-detect the two core changes.
  - `uses_messages_api(model_id)`: true for `claude-*` ids (also behind `anthropic/`), except `-fast` variants, when both core changes are present, the configured base URL (`COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`, else a Copilot `model.base_url`, else the default) and every host a token exchange handed out are Copilot hosts, and no legacy `model.api_mode` is saved for that model as the default. Swallowed read errors are logged at debug, and the module docstring lists every read the wire choice makes.
  - The exchanged-host check reads every in-memory exchange (env token or pool row), or the persisted exchange file read-only before the first exchange; it validates no token and fails closed when the cache or a persisted store that exists can't be read (corrupt or over the size cap), and an unreadable configured base URL also keeps Claude on `chat_completions`.
  - The legacy-pin check reads the default the way core does (`model.model` alias, dict default) and compares ids after the plugin's catalog-free normalization, so a dashed `claude-sonnet-4-6` default matches the dotted id `/model` and resume use.
  - `_api_mode_for_id()`, shared by both `api_mode_for_model` paths: GPT-5+ except `gpt-5-mini` → `codex_responses`, Claude → `anthropic_messages` (as above), else `chat_completions`.
  - `anthropic_auth_style(*, base_url)`: `"bearer"` for `githubcopilot.com` hosts, else `None`.
  - On a core without the fix, a saved `model.api_mode: anthropic_messages` (which that core applies to every Copilot model) is reported once with how to remove it.
- `github-copilot/copilot/setup.py`: `hermes model` → GitHub Copilot no longer saves `model.api_mode`, and removes one an earlier setup saved from the user's own `config.yaml` (read raw, so a managed-overlay value is never re-saved).
- `github-copilot/README.md`: a "Claude on `/v1/messages`" section (both core requirements, the cache benefit, proxies, `-fast` variants, what the wire choice reads, saved `api_mode`). `plugin.yaml` 1.1.0.
- `github-copilot/tests/conftest.py`: `offline_messages_turn()`, one real `AIAgent.chat` turn with every httpx transport replaced by an `httpx.MockTransport`, returning the requests as sent; it can fail the first request with a given status.
- `github-copilot/tests/test_copilot_messages_route.py` (new): routing per model family; the fallbacks without either core change and with a proxy base URL (env, config, an in-memory exchange from any credential, or the persisted exchange); fail-closed and no-token-lookup checks; host-anchored `anthropic_auth_style`; a wire-level turn (`POST /v1/messages`, `Authorization: Bearer`, no `x-api-key`, the wire model id, editor headers, `x-initiator`, no `Copilot-Vision-Request`); an offline 401 → 200 turn whose retry carries `Bearer <fresh token>` and the Copilot headers; and setup saving no `api_mode`.
- `github-copilot/tests/test_copilot_saved_api_mode.py` (new): every saved value on a core with the fix (one saved for a GPT default never pins Claude; a saved `anthropic_messages` for a Claude default leaves GPT targets on their own wire; a legacy value for a Claude default keeps only that model on `chat_completions`, across id spellings and config shapes) and without it (Claude never answers `anthropic_messages`; a saved `anthropic_messages` is reported once).

## Safety

- **Other models are unchanged.** GPT-5+ still uses Responses; GPT-4.x, Gemini and the rest still use Chat Completions.
- **Older core:** without the seam or the saved-`api_mode` fix, Claude stays on `chat_completions`. Without the seam core would send the Copilot token as `x-api-key`; without the fix a `/model --global` Claude pick would save `anthropic_messages`, which that core applies to every Copilot model, breaking GPT targets (delegation, cron, auxiliary tasks).
- **Proxies:** a non-Copilot `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`, `model.base_url` or exchanged host keeps Claude on `chat_completions` (tested), and an unreadable exchange cache, persisted exchange store or base-URL lookup does too. A proxy set only for one session (`/model`, gateway or Desktop override) isn't seen when the wire is chosen; the README says to set it in `model.base_url` / `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`.
- **Reserved headers:** core filters `client_headers` on this path and never asks about hosts whose auth it owns, non-ASCII hosts, or cleartext URLs that aren't strictly local; see the seam PR.
- **Lookalike hosts:** `api.githubcopilot.com.evil.test` and `evil.test/api.githubcopilot.com` get `None` (tested).
- **No vision header needed:** `/v1/messages` accepted image blocks without `Copilot-Vision-Request` (live, 16px and 256px PNGs).
- **Saved `api_mode`:** with the core fix, a saved value applies only to the saved default, and `/model --global` or a Desktop pick no longer saves one. If an earlier setup saved `chat_completions` or `codex_responses` and the default is a Claude model, that model stays on `chat_completions` on every path (startup and `/model` agree); other Claude models use `/v1/messages`. `hermes model` or `hermes config unset model.api_mode` moves the default too; the README says so.
- **No network call to choose the wire:** it reads the env, the cached config and the exchange cache; normalizing the model id may read the account's cached live catalog (README).

## Tests

`python -m pytest -q` in `github-copilot/`, with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a hermes-agent checkout:

- Both core PRs merged together: **199 passed**.
- The seam PR only: **161 passed, 38 skipped**.
- The fix PR only: **157 passed, 42 skipped**.
- hermes-agent `main`: **157 passed, 42 skipped**.

Every skip names the missing core change, and the fallback tests pass on every core.

## Live verification

Rows used `claude-sonnet-5.5` against `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/messages` unless a row says otherwise, with `Authorization: Bearer` and no `x-api-key`; HTTP 200 unless noted. On an earlier version of this branch plus an earlier version of the seam PR, before their last review rounds (the route now also requires the fix PR; none of the later changes alters the requests sent on the route for a config without a saved `api_mode`, as used here):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Every Claude id in my catalog | Sent with core's hyphenated id (`max_tokens` 5): `claude-fable-5.1`, `claude-haiku-5.5`, `claude-opus-4.8`, `claude-opus-5.5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4.5` answered. `claude-opus-4.8-fast` (preview) returned 400 `model_not_supported` for `claude-opus-4-8-fast`, so it stays on `/chat/completions`, where it answered. |
| Long context | `claude-haiku-5.5`, 252,637 input tokens accepted without the 1M beta; the catalog lists no `-1m` ids. |
| Agent turns | No `model.api_mode` in config: plain turn `pong` and a 2-call tool turn on `anthropic_messages`, 1h cache markers sent, `x-initiator` `user` then `agent` |

Earlier runs (this branch's first commits plus an earlier core seam):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plain / tool / streaming | `pong` with 866 tokens written to the 1h cache; tool answer in 2 calls (second read 3,523 cached); streamed `1, 2, 3, 4, 5` |
| Reasoning effort | Adaptive thinking with `output_config.effort: low`; correct answer (391) |
| Image | 16px PNG "Red."; 256px two-color PNG "Red, blue." |
| Two-turn cache | Turn 1 wrote 11,632 tokens (1h); turn 2 read 11,632 |
| Real session, idle gap | `claude-opus-5.5`, ~558K tokens: first call after the switch `write=495,587`; after a 12-minute gap the next call read **557,667 of 558,377** from cache; earlier on `/chat/completions`, a call after a 16-minute gap read none of 510,419. |

## Related

- #56: the problem report, with the follow-up comment proposing this core-seam + plugin split.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#146877: required Anthropic auth-style seam.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#146876: required saved-`api_mode` fix (a bug on `main` on its own).
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#49184 by @arminanton: prior art for routing Copilot Claude to `/v1/messages` with Bearer auth, closed when Copilot moved into this plugin; thanks for the original analysis.
- #40 (Claude on Copilot drops `reasoning_effort`): on this route, effort reached the wire as `output_config.effort` above; I haven't verified whether that fully resolves #40.
- #46 (long-context tiers hidden without `X-GitHub-Api-Version`): separate catalog issue. On `/v1/messages`, a ~429K-token prompt was accepted with neither the 1M beta nor `X-GitHub-Api-Version`; with `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-08-01`, the catalog reports 1M-token windows for these Claude ids (`claude-haiku-4.5`: 200K).
- Possible core follow-ups: keeping dotted ids on the Anthropic wire (like `_anthropic_preserve_dots`) would let `-fast` variants use `/v1/messages`, and passing the live base URL to `api_mode_for_model` would cover per-session proxies.

title: feat(github-copilot): record Copilot's reported cost per call, estimate otherwise
body:
## Summary

Hermes records every GitHub Copilot call with cost status `unknown` and no amount: core has no Copilot rate card. This PR makes `CopilotProfile.get_usage_cost` return the amount Copilot itself reports for each call, as `actual`, and otherwise falls back to an estimate at the model vendor's list rate.

**Needs one hermes-agent PR for the reported cost; the other is optional.** NousResearch/hermes-agent#148019 adds `ProviderProfile.usage_response_fields` so a profile can name top-level response fields core should carry into `usage.raw_usage`. With it, the profile declares `copilot_usage` and records Copilot's reported cost, for main-loop and auxiliary calls. Without it (current `main`), the profile declares nothing and records the vendor-list-rate estimate. This PR is safe to merge before or after it.

NousResearch/hermes-agent#148020 is optional and independent of both: it stores an `actual` amount in `actual_cost_usd` instead of `estimated_cost_usd` and makes every spend reader add the two columns. It changes where the reported amount is stored, not whether this plugin reports it.

It is independent of #57 (Claude on `/v1/messages`): the two share no files and merge cleanly in either order. With #57, Claude on `/v1/messages` also gets 1h cache writes priced correctly in the fallback estimate.

## Why

Copilot responses carry a top-level `copilot_usage` object next to `usage`: per-bucket `token_details` (`input`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `output`, each with `token_count`, `batch_size` and `cost_per_batch`) and `total_nano_aiu`, which on every recorded sample equals the sum of `token_count × cost_per_batch / batch_size` over the buckets. I checked all three wires the plugin uses, streamed and not: the object is on the response body for `/chat/completions`, `/responses` and `/v1/messages`; when streaming it rides on the final usage chunk (chat completions), the `response.completed` event (Responses), and the `message_delta` event (Anthropic Messages).

The plugin reads `total_nano_aiu / 1e11` as the call's charge in USD. GitHub doesn't document this response field, so the conversion is inferred: GitHub's docs give the unit (nano-AI units; the Copilot SDK guide converts 1e9 nano-AIU to one AI credit) and price one AI credit at USD 0.01, and on every recorded sample the per-token rates this conversion implies equal the vendor list rates in core's tables for that model.

The reported amount is better than any table estimate: it is what Copilot charged for the call, it includes cache writes that the OpenAI-shaped `usage` on `/chat/completions` doesn't report, and it stays correct when Copilot's rates differ from a vendor's list price or change.

## What changes

- `github-copilot/copilot/__init__.py`: `CopilotProfile.get_usage_cost` (accepts extra keyword context, so a core that passes `base_url`, as NousResearch/hermes-agent#128429 proposes, keeps working and can tell GitHub Models apart); the profile declares `usage_response_fields=("copilot_usage",)` only when core's `ProviderProfile` has that field.
- `github-copilot/copilot/pricing.py` (new):
  - Reported cost: `copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu` from `usage.raw_usage`, when it is a whole number (an int or an integral float) from 0 to 1e14 (USD 1000 for one call), becomes `amount = total / 1e11`, status `actual`, source `provider_cost_api`, an exact label (no `~`), note `GitHub-reported cost (copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu)`. Anything else (negative, fractional, infinite, NaN, boolean, a string, or above the bound) falls back to the estimate.
  - Fallback estimate: Claude at Anthropic's list rates and GPT / `o`-series at OpenAI's, through core's own tables (Copilot's dotted id first, then the vendor's dashed id); 1h cache writes (`usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`) at 2x input; a model neither id prices uses a small hand-kept table of rates read from Copilot's `cost_per_batch` (today only `claude-sonnet-5.5`, which core's snapshot lacks; source `custom_contract`); a model with no known vendor rate returns `None`, so core keeps reporting `unknown`.
- `github-copilot/copilot/catalog.py`: `_is_github_models_host()`, true only for a known `models.github.ai` URL.
- `github-copilot/tests/test_copilot_reported_cost.py` (new): recorded `copilot_usage` samples for all three wires, malformed and out-of-range totals (including `10**320`, `1e300`, `10**15`), whole totals up to the bound, the GitHub Models handling, the field declaration per core, core's capture into the hook, and three offline streamed `AIAgent` turns through core's real stream paths (chat completions usage chunk, Responses `response.completed`, Anthropic `message_delta` through the Anthropic SDK) recorded as `actual`.
- `github-copilot/tests/test_copilot_usage_cost.py` (new): the fallback estimate (rates, 1h writes, long-context tier, dashed ids, observed-rate fallback, unknown models, failure handling).

## Testing

`python -m pytest -q` in `github-copilot/`, with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a hermes-agent checkout:

- With NousResearch/hermes-agent#148019: **188 passed**.
- With #148019 and #148020 merged together: **188 passed**.
- hermes-agent `main`: **184 passed, 4 skipped** (the 4 tests that need `ProviderProfile.usage_response_fields` in hermes-agent).

## Compatibility

- **Older core:** no `usage_response_fields`, so the profile declares nothing; Claude and GPT calls that core's tables can price are recorded at the vendor-list-rate estimate (status `estimated`) instead of `unknown`, and other models stay `unknown`.
- **Response without the field** (or a malformed or out-of-range total): the estimate applies.
- **Failures never break a turn:** `get_usage_cost` returns `None` on any pricing error or a pricing module that fails to import, and core prices the call as if the hook weren't there.
- **GitHub Models:** the `github-models` aliases (`models.github.ai`) share this profile. I haven't checked whether those responses carry `copilot_usage`. Today's core doesn't pass the request URL to the hook, so the profile can't tell the hosts apart: a GitHub Models call without a reported amount gets the same vendor-list-rate estimate, the notes say "GitHub-reported" rather than naming a product, and the estimate's note says GitHub Models routes may bill differently. A core that passes `base_url` lets such a call skip the Copilot-rate estimate (core pricing applies instead); a reported amount is still recorded.
- `plugin.yaml` is unchanged (no version bump), so this doesn't collide with #57.

## Risks

- The fallback estimate is vendor list price. For the Claude and GPT models I compared (`claude-sonnet-5`, `gpt-6.1-sol`), core's list rates match the per-token rates Copilot reports; other models aren't checked.
- The `/1e11` conversion is inferred (see Why); a change in Copilot's units would show up as reported amounts that no longer match the per-bucket rates.
- A reported total of 0 is recorded as an `actual` zero, by design: it is what Copilot reported for the call, and the plugin doesn't second-guess a well-formed report with an estimate.
- On plans with an included AI-credit allowance, the reported amount draws down that allowance before anything is billed; it's recorded as `actual` because it is the call's charge as Copilot reports it, not necessarily out-of-pocket spend.

## Live verification

In-process `AIAgent` turns against GitHub Copilot with this branch and NousResearch/hermes-agent#148019 and #148020 merged together, in an isolated Hermes home, through a local pass-through proxy that adds the Copilot credential, one turn per wire, streamed and non-streamed: `claude-sonnet-5` on `chat_completions` and `anthropic_messages`, `gpt-6.1-sol` on `codex_responses`. In all six, the main-loop call was recorded with `cost_status = actual`, `cost_source = provider_cost_api`, and an amount equal to that response's `copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu / 1e11`, on the agent and in `actual_cost_usd` (with `estimated_cost_usd` at 0) on the session row in `state.db`. A guard in the script refused every non-local host, and no call tried one. This run doesn't verify auxiliary calls: title generation went to the local proxy as a custom endpoint, so it wasn't priced through this profile (it was recorded as `unknown`). Auxiliary capture is covered by #148019's tests.

## Related

- #56, #57: the Claude `/v1/messages` route; independent of this PR.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#148019: the core field this PR needs for the reported cost; without it the estimate applies.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#148020: optional; stores `actual` amounts in `actual_cost_usd`.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#128429: passes `base_url` to `get_usage_cost`; this profile already accepts it and uses it to tell GitHub Models apart.

title: inbox: add `--decisions` — decisions waiting on the operator, with recommendation and risk
body:
**Problem**
`hermes inbox` is the best single view of what's in flight. But for an operator running many agents, the most important question is "what is waiting on *me*, and what should I pick?" Today inbox answers that with card titles only. On my profile today it shows 33 attention items. About 20 are failed cron runs, and the ~8 real human decisions are buried among them, each with nothing more than a title. To decide, I have to open every card.

**Proposal**
Add `hermes inbox --decisions` (plus a `decisions` key in `--json`) listing blocked kanban tasks that need a human. Each item shows:

- Decision — the one question, with the exact reply words
- Recommendation — the agent's pick
- Why + confidence %
- Risk if you do / risk if you don't
- Deadline (real, optional)

Sorted by deadline, then age. Failed crons and undelivered delegations stay in their own section so they don't bury decisions.

**How the fields get there (no schema change)**
A plain-text block in the task body or a comment; the newest block wins:

```
DECISION BLOCK
Decision: Send the first weekly email Thursday? Reply "send" or "hold".
Recommendation: send
Why + Confidence: sample rendered and unsubscribe works. Confidence: 80%
Risk if you do: a formatting slip reaches subscribers once
Risk if you don't: no email this week; zero cost
Deadline: 2026-11-05 07:00 CT
END DECISION BLOCK
```

A task counts as "needs a human" when it is blocked with `kind=needs_input` (or carries a configurable title tag). If the block is missing, the item renders as **INCOMPLETE**, which nudges the owning agent to supply it rather than leaving the human to dig.

**Prior art / related**
- #7 (@RohiRIK, durable observations / local attention / Herald threads) makes attention items durable and actionable. This proposal is complementary: it adds the *decision content* those items lack, and could sit on #7's attention model.
- #5 (Adopt: inbox): Nous said inbox stays maintained, so this is offered as a small, opt-in extension rather than a new plugin.

**Evidence it's useful**
I run this today as a local script that reads `hermes inbox --json` plus the kanban DBs read-only and renders one HTML page every 10 min. It turned 33 undifferentiated attention lines into 11 decisions, one card each, plus a separate "systems broken" list. I'm happy to turn it into a PR against `inbox/` (collector + `--decisions` flag + tests) if the shape is welcome.

**Open questions for maintainers**
1. Block in body/comment text, or a structured field on the task?
2. Trigger on `needs_input` blocks only, or also a configurable tag?
3. Text output only, or also an optional `--html` render?

title: feat(patsnap): patent and literature search through Patsnap's hosted MCP server
body:
Adds a `patsnap` Labs plugin. It lets Hermes search patents and scientific papers through Patsnap's own hosted MCP server, using the user's `PATSNAP_API_KEY`. Teknium asked for it to live here instead of in the core MCP catalog, which is being removed (hermes-agent#85138).

## What it ships
- `patsnap/mcp.json`: one `streamable-http` server named `patsnap` at `https://connect.patsnap.com/2b0355/logic-mcp`. The key goes in an `apikey` header as `${PATSNAP_API_KEY}`, filled from the profile's `.env` / secret source when Hermes connects. It is never put in the URL.
- `patsnap/plugin.json`: Agent Plugins v1 manifest. Its `config_schema` adds a Patsnap API key secret field (`env: PATSNAP_API_KEY`), so Desktop's Settings → Plugins shows a key field.
- `patsnap/skills/patsnap-search/`: a workflow skill covering when to use each of the 9 server tools, the strategy/parameter rules, assignee resolution, keeping credit use low, and stopping on an auth error.
- `patsnap/README.md`: install, how the key is sent, tool list, disclosure, attribution (server is Patsnap's, Apache-2.0).
- Root README: one row in the plugin table.

### Why hosted HTTP and not the stdio bridge
The old core manifest launched Patsnap's Node bridge from a git checkout (`npm ci` + `node src/index.js`). The bridge does nothing but forward to this same hosted endpoint, and it puts the key in the URL query string (`?apikey=`). The hosted endpoint also accepts the key as an `apikey` header (checked live, below). Going direct means:
- no Node, no `npm ci`, no code from a third-party checkout;
- the key stays out of URLs and logs;
- Hermes strips the header on any cross-origin redirect (`strict_redirect_headers`).

## Evidence (scratch `HERMES_HOME`, `git archive origin/main` of hermes-agent)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins validate patsnap` | portable manifest ✓, config schema ✓, security scan **safe**, "portable plugin (no Python)". Passed |
| `hermes plugins install file://<clone>#patsnap --enable --yes-deps` | rc 0, installed + enabled |
| `get_portable_mcp_servers()` | `patsnap: {url: …/logic-mcp, strict_redirect_headers: true, headers: {apikey: ${PATSNAP_API_KEY}}}` |
| disable / enable | `[]` / `['patsnap']` |
| no key in `.env` | does not connect: `${PATSNAP_API_KEY} in url/headers is not set in this profile's .env or secret source` |
| placeholder key in `.env` | real `POST https://connect.patsnap.com/2b0355/logic-mcp` → Patsnap's own `Access token expired or authentication error!`, so the header is filled in and sent |
| endpoint, curl | no credential → 401 `no access token provided`; `apikey:` header → JSON-RPC auth error (header accepted); `Authorization: Bearer` / `x-api-key` → 401 (not accepted) |

**NOT_COVERED:**
- `tools/list` and a real search: there's no Patsnap key on the host, and the hosted server requires one to `initialize`. The 9 tool names come from Patsnap's published tool guide.
- A real model turn: same reason.

**Core issue this exposed (not in this plugin):** the first connect fills in the header correctly. But when a remote MCP server that came from a plugin rebuilds its connection (any retry or reconnect), `_refresh_remote_config` re-reads the entry without filling in `${VAR}`. The header is then seen as "changed", and the server parks on `${PATSNAP_API_KEY} … is not set`.
- Live check: wrapping that read in `_interpolate_env_vars` makes all 3 retries reach Patsnap.
- Impact: with a real key the first connect works, so this only shows up after a dropped connection.
- Fixed in its own core PR: NousResearch/hermes-agent#148879.

## Catalog
The core entry `plugin-catalog/patsnap.yaml` (`tier: community`, `subdir: patsnap`) is in hermes-agent#85138. It pins this PR's head for now. Re-pin it to this repo's merge commit once this lands (a rebase merge rewrites SHAs).

title: github-copilot: pool-only login (`hermes auth add copilot`) invisible to aux/fallback resolver — `resolve_api_key_secret()` returns ("","") instead of None
body:
Environment: Hermes v0.22.6 (2026.9.24), github-copilot plugin 1.0.0

## Summary
With Copilot signed in only via `hermes auth add copilot` (credential pool, no `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var), `hermes chat --provider copilot` works, but `resolve_provider_client("copilot")` returns `(None, None)`. The fallback chain therefore skips Copilot with `Fallback to copilot failed: provider not configured`.

## Cause
- Core `hermes_cli/auth.py::_resolve_api_key_provider_secret` order: provider-owned `profile.resolve_api_key_secret()` (final if not None) -> env vars -> credential pool ("Fallback: credential pool (e.g. zai key stored via auth.json)").
- Contract in `providers/base.py`: `resolve_api_key_secret()` "None = generic env/pool ladder".
- The plugin's `copilot/credentials.py::CopilotProfile.resolve_api_key_secret` only consults `resolve_copilot_token()` (env vars only). With no env token it returns `("", "")`, not None, so core treats it as a final "no key" and never reaches the pool step.

## Repro
1. Remove all of COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN.
2. `hermes auth add copilot` (device code); `hermes auth list` shows the entry.
3. Config: `fallback_providers: [{provider: copilot, model: gpt-6.1-terra}]`, primary anthropic.
4. Force the primary to fail (e.g. `hermes chat -q hi --provider anthropic -m claude-nonexistent-9`).
5. Log: `Fallback to copilot failed: provider not configured`.
6. Direct: `resolve_provider_client('copilot', model='gpt-6.1-terra')` -> `(None, None)`; DEBUG: `provider copilot has no API key configured (tried: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN)`.

## Expected
Pool-only login resolves in the aux/fallback path, as it does for other api_key providers.

## Suggested fix (either)
- Plugin: return None from `resolve_api_key_secret` when no env token is found (let the generic ladder reach the pool), or read the pool itself.
- Core: treat an empty api_key from the provider-owned result as fall-through rather than final.

## Workaround
Copy the pool token into `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` in `~/.hermes/.env`. Forced failover then logs `Fallback activated: ... -> gpt-6.1-terra (copilot)`.

## Notes
- Likely also affects title generation / compression aux calls on pool-only setups (not verified).
- Not found in open issues of NousResearch/hermes-agent or hermes-labs-plugins; nearest: hermes-agent #148536 (different symptom, same class: status vs. runtime resolve credentials differently).

title: fix(github-copilot): defer to the credential pool when no env token is set
body:
`resolve_api_key_secret()` returned `("", "")` when no `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` was set. Core treats a non-None result as final, so a pool-only login (`hermes auth add copilot`) never reached the credential pool and `resolve_provider_client("copilot")` returned `(None, None)`; the fallback chain logged "provider not configured".

It now returns `None` when there is no env token, so core's generic ladder reaches the pool. Behavior with an env token is unchanged.

Updated the existing assertion in `test_rule11_no_cli_credentials.py` (`secret is None`). Full github-copilot suite: 144 passed on Python 3.14 against current hermes-agent.

Fixes #61.

title: github-copilot: fine-grained PAT gets HTTP 400 (vscode-chat integration id)
body:
With `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` set to a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_*`, Copilot Requests permission, which `setup.py` and `credentials.py` list as supported), every request the plugin builds with `copilot_request_headers()` sends `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat`. GitHub rejects that for a PAT: `GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` returns 400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"; the same request with `copilot-developer-cli` returns 200 (also on `api.business.githubcopilot.com`).

The catalog falls back to the static list, and image turns fail, because core merges the `client_headers(has_images=True)` answer over the configured headers (a `model.default_headers.Copilot-Integration-Id` set by the user doesn't help there). The token exchange returns 404 for a PAT, so the raw PAT is the bearer and no exchanged token avoids it.

**Versions:** hermes-agent v0.22.7, github-copilot plugin at `346cfe9` (current `main` for `github-copilot/`).

**Reproduce** (status codes only; Copilot Business seat):

```sh
for id in vscode-chat copilot-developer-cli; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$id %{http_code}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    -H "Copilot-Integration-Id: $id" \
    https://api.githubcopilot.com/models
done
# vscode-chat 400
# copilot-developer-cli 200
```

**Fix:** choose the id from the token (`copilot-developer-cli` for `github_pat_`) in `copilot_request_headers()`, and pass `api_key` through `fetch_github_model_catalog` and the `client_headers` hook. OAuth and exchanged tokens keep `vscode-chat`.

We carry this as a patch with tests (`tests/test_copilot_pat_integration_id.py`: client headers with and without images, the catalog request, an offline chat turn; they fail on `346cfe9` and pass with the patch; the plugin's full suite passes): https://github.com/Faraclas/adaptive-overlay/blob/630361c099f3e9763e9d4f68149db13d8f466dea/app-ai/hermes-agent/files/hermes-agent-copilot-plugin-pat-integration-id.patch

Happy to open it as a PR if that's preferred.

Related but different: #43 (exchange 404 on Individual plans), #48 (a classic `ghp_` token picked from the credential pool).

title: yuanbao: Tencent Yuanbao platform + yb_* tools move here from hermes-agent core (history kept)
body:
Moves the Tencent Yuanbao messaging platform and its `yb_*` tools out of hermes-agent core into this repo as the `yuanbao` plugin.

> Yuanbao is now a Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported, and likely not maintained going forward. Fixes from the community are welcome.

Core removal PR: NousResearch/hermes-agent#150210 (adds the LEFT_CORE row that installs this plugin for homes that used Yuanbao).

## What moved

| From hermes-agent | To |
|---|---|
| `plugins/platforms/yuanbao/` (and older `gateway/platforms/yuanbao*.py`) | `yuanbao/` |
| `tools/yuanbao_tools.py` | `yuanbao/tools.py` |
| `tests/**/test_yuanbao_*.py` (12 files) | `yuanbao/tests/` |

Full history is kept. `git filter-repo` covered every path Yuanbao has had in core up to `b2e4ded57c7`: 136 commits by 24 authors, with commit-message issue refs pointing at `NousResearch/hermes-agent#N`. The imported tree is byte-identical to core at that sha (`177cdcb`). The packaging is one commit on top (`9ee7cb4`), and the card + README row is a separate docs commit. On top of that come 12 open community fixes from the stranded core backlog, each under its contributor's authorship (table below).

None of the names existing installs rely on change: platform `yuanbao`, toolset `yuanbao`, tools `yb_query_group_info` / `yb_query_group_members` / `yb_send_dm` / `yb_search_sticker` / `yb_send_sticker`, every `YUANBAO_*` env var, `platforms.yuanbao` (and the legacy `gateway.yuanbao`) config keys, and `YUANBAO_HOME_CHANNEL`. Core's composite `hermes-yuanbao` toolset goes away with core, as `hermes-homeassistant` did.

## Packaging

- **Manifest:** `name: yuanbao`, homepage, `kind: platform`, `provides_tools` = the 5 `yb_*` names. `requires_env` / `optional_env` are exactly what core had. `websockets>=15.0.1,<16` goes in `pyproject.toml`.
- **`register()`:** calls `ctx.register_platform` with optional `PlatformEntry` kwargs, each passed only when the running core has that field (`_OPTIONAL_ENTRY_KWARGS`, as in homeassistant), then `ctx.register_tool` for the `yuanbao` toolset.
- **Inert on cores that still bundle Yuanbao.** The guard looks for `plugins/platforms/yuanbao` or `tools/yuanbao_tools.py` with `importlib.machinery.PathFinder`, searching only those packages' own `__path__`. A namespace-only leftover such as `__pycache__` does not count. When it finds core's copy, the plugin logs one INFO line and registers nothing.
- **One adapter class object:** adapter, tools and standalone sender import each other relatively, so `YuanbaoAdapter.get_active()` in the tools returns the instance the gateway registry created (tested).
- **`platform_hint`:** core's adapter hint byte-for-byte (main's `register.py` text, 715 chars). The DM guidance from core's `gateway/session.py` "Platform notes" line now sits in the `yb_send_dm` description, so it reaches neither cron prompts nor a `platform_hints` replace.
- **Skill:** core's `optional-skills/yuanbao/SKILL.md` moved in unchanged as `yuanbao/skills/yuanbao/SKILL.md`. It is registered as `yuanbao:yuanbao` through `ctx.register_skill`, only when the plugin is active. The core PR drops its copy.
- **`Platform.YUANBAO` becomes `Platform("yuanbao")` at call time.** The env bridge moves from an import-time `EnvCred` row to `env_enablement_fn` with the same keys. Live parity check: from the same env, core-with-bundled-copy and core-without (plugin) produce a byte-identical `platforms.yuanbao`, covering app id via legacy `YUANBAO_APP_KEY`, policies, ws_url, route_env and home channel.
- **Private imports `validate` flagged are replaced:**
  - `agent.i18n.t` → a local `_i18n.py` with core's 3 strings in all 17 languages; core deletes those locale keys.
  - `hermes_cli.gateway` helpers → the public setup-wizard helpers and `get_scoped_secret`.
  - `TranscriptReadError` → imported via `gateway.platforms.base`.
  - `EnvCred` / `strip_lower` → local code.
  - Still flagged, with no public seam: `hermes_cli.version_info` (sign-token headers), `gateway.pairing.PairingStore` (pairing-approved home channel) and `gateway.platforms.send_targets` (send-contract types).
- **Tests:** core's suite ported with import paths rewritten. The conftest is modelled on homeassistant's (package alias, real `PlatformEntry` registered up front, root collected as a plain Dir, autouse temp `HERMES_HOME` with `YUANBAO_*` cleared). `test_plugin_packaging.py` covers the toolset, the skill, hint bytes, target syntax, env bridge through the real `load_gateway_config`, localized strings and the guard.
- **README:** labs header, the unsupported notice, and setup copied from core's docs page. `LICENSE` / `.gitignore` / `pytest.ini` come from telegram-business. Card: `assets/yuanbao.jpg`.

## Ported community fixes

Twelve open hermes-agent PRs aimed at Yuanbao could never merge into core after the move. Each was ported here with its author kept, from hermes-agent branch `port/yuanbao-backlog` (cherry-picked onto `b2e4ded`, 248 core tests green there). Paths were rewritten `plugins/platforms/yuanbao/` → `yuanbao/` and `tests/**/test_yuanbao_*` → `yuanbao/tests/`, imports were moved to the plugin's shape (relative imports, `Platform("yuanbao")`, the `yuanbao_plugin` test alias), and the commits were applied with `git am`. Duplicate PRs get `Co-authored-by` credit.

| Core PR | Author | Fixes | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| #58798 (+ dup #61539/#61540) | @ooiuuii (co: @ms-alan) | `image/gif; charset=binary` or an uppercase MIME gave image_format 255 and skipped dimension parsing in `upload_to_cos` | `278b53c` |
| #52783 (+ dup #56719/#64062/#77808) | @annguyenNous (co: @AlexFucuson9, @RelaxJonh) | upload-checksum md5 now passes `usedforsecurity=False` (FIPS hosts); the SHA-1 HMAC signing input is left alone | `4944896` |
| #56927 | @solyanviktor-star | the `download_url` redirect guard never fired (`response.next_request` is None in an httpx response hook); it now reads Location | `178f6c4` |
| #145139 | @Muzzy5150 | debounce and group queues are bounded under sustained inbound load (new `inbound_capacity.py`) | `858795a` |
| #122726 | @liuhao1024 | a system SOCKS proxy that websockets picks up but cannot dial (no python-socks) is swapped for the HTTP(S) proxy or a direct dial (new `ws_proxy.py`) | `b963b8e` |
| #127912 (+ #72296 Yuanbao half) | @jonpol01 (co: @Frowtek) | a nickname with `\|`, `]` or a newline can no longer forge a `[name\|id]` attribution line (observed, @bot and forwarded paths) | `ce8575f` |
| #107241 (partial) | @KoNit-K | a send ACK with a business error code (e.g. 999) now counts as a failed delivery, not a success (new `send_ack.py`); text chunk limit is 1200, matching Yuanbao's own plugin. The "refuse unsplittable chunk" hunk and stale-merge reverts were not taken | `370996a` |
| #83418 (partial) | @briandevans | the reconnect task is anchored via `_track_task`, so it cannot be GC'd mid-backoff (the disconnect drain is already done by the gateway's `cancel_background_tasks()`) | `9bae476` |
| #60324 (adapted) | @hizzgdev (PR by @zzgbot) | outbound `@nickname` went out as plain text because nothing filled the member cache; the send path refreshes it when the text has a mention | `98ecac9` |
| #74860 (Yuanbao half) | @pierrenode | home-channel designation read the default profile's pairing store; it now uses the adapter's owner profile | `258fea2` |
| #118106 (Yuanbao half) | @smalever | observed/recall transcript rows used ISO timestamps that `coerce_epoch` rejects with a warning per message; they are epoch floats now | `d7f98ba` |
| #78166 | @iacker | an @bot group message queued behind the active turn and could not interrupt it; re-applied on #145139's bounded dispatch | `88c8938` |

Also: `e7811fd` copies core's `tests/waiting.py` helper into `yuanbao/tests/` and lets sibling test helpers import by module name, since the ported tests used `tests.waiting` / `tests.gateway.test_yuanbao_pipeline`. `82c6d46` is the README half of #65073 (@briandevans, credited): verbose logging is `hermes gateway run -vv`, because Hermes never reads `HERMES_LOG_LEVEL`. Every commit in the series passes the suite on the removed tree on its own.

Not ported (verdicts in the backlog triage): #22340 and #55782 are already fixed on main. #104315 (reconnect on 4014) would make two gateways on one bot evict each other in a loop, and Yuanbao's own plugin never reconnects on that code. #29077 and #137350 are features. #50359 holds stale coverage tests. The MIXED core PRs keep their core halves in hermes-agent.

## Review fixes

Fixes from the independent review of `82c6d46`. Every fix has a test that fails at `82c6d46`.

| Finding | Fix | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| A profile clone kept `YUANBAO_*` credentials. `shared_env_prefixes=("YUANBAO_",)` claimed the yb_* tools read that env, which they do not, and a legacy `APP_KEY` source counted as "not running" | Dropped the prefix. A channel-less clone strips every `YUANBAO_*` key again, as core did | `23ed01f` |
| The session "Platform notes" line in `platform_hint` reached cron prompts, and a `platform_hints` replace dropped it | Hint = main's bytes. DM-vs-group-reply guidance moved to the `yb_send_dm` description | `2b0781e` |
| A body line could open with a forged `[name\|id]` header (@bot path, observed path, forwarded records) | A header-shaped body line gets its `[` escaped as `\[` (leading blanks and zero-width characters included). Other lines are unchanged. The test docstring now says what is guaranteed | `6a8343e`, `67fd906` |
| Private `_owner_transport_profile` called unguarded | `getattr` with a fallback to `_owner_profile`. Same result when the method exists | `7844d39` |
| Tests import private core tables | One parametrized case per table, using `getattr` + skip when the name is absent | `21934d4` |
| `_fetch_resource_url` followed redirects with `X-Token` | `follow_redirects=False`: the JSON API treats a 3xx as a failure. Tested with loopback servers | `a578a0c` |
| Core's optional `yuanbao` skill is left behind when the tools move | Moved into the plugin as `yuanbao:yuanbao`, registered behind the inert guard. Co-authored-by the original authors | `6386833` |
| The inert guard checks for core's files, not whether core's adapter is enabled | Documented in the README (fails safe on old cores) | `fbfab49` |

## Second review fixes

Fixes from the independent review of `67fd906`. Each fix has a test that fails at `67fd906`.

| Finding | Fix | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| The single WebSocket reader awaited inbound admission capacity (from `858795a`, port of hermes-agent#145139). With 64 pushes retained, it stopped reading PONGs and RPC responses, causing false heartbeat timeouts and stalled sends | The reader resolves control frames at once and passes inbound pushes to a bounded FIFO (64 frames / 4 MiB) that one admitter task drains. #145139's intent holds: bounded memory, FIFO admission, PushAck only after admission. A push that arrives while the FIFO is full is shed without an ACK and counted in a warning, so the server redelivers it | `bf93e45` |
| An addressed group follow-up overwrote the recall tracking before core decided to queue it (from `88c8938`, port of #78166). Recalling the running message did not interrupt it, and recalling the queued follow-up interrupted the running turn instead | Recall id/text are recorded when core actually starts that message's turn (`_process_message_background`). Recalling a queued, unmerged follow-up drops it and leaves the running turn alone | `180e428` |
| README disclosure listed only Tencent endpoints | Adds the public media URL downloads (messages, quoted replies, send-tool URLs; SSRF-checked, size-capped). Also states that sign-token / AUTH_BIND carry the Hermes version, OS name and a fixed instance id `17`, which is the same on every install | `a178086` |

## Expected red until the core PR lands

This PR's `validate` on hermes-agent `main` fails `built-in tool collisions` (the 5 `yb_*` names are still built-ins there), so CI's pytest step is skipped. That is by design for a move of built-in tools: the declared `provides_tools` stays truthful. The same validate is green against the core PR's tree (table below).

**Merge order:** hermes-agent#150210 (core removal) → re-run this PR's CI (green) → this PR → data-only catalog PR at the merged sha. No `requires_hermes` floor until a stable release carries the core removal; the inert guard covers older cores.

## Gates

Python 3.14 test env, `env -i` with a scratch HOME. Core trees come from `git archive`.

| Gate | Tree | Result |

title: fix(github-copilot): resolve reasoning efforts from live catalog
body:
Fixes #40

## Problem
Claude, Gemini and GPT-6.x on Copilot silently drop the configured `reasoning_effort`: requests go out with no `reasoning` field, although the Copilot `/models` catalog advertises `capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort` for them.

## Root cause
`build_api_kwargs_extras` and `reasoning_payload` call `github_model_reasoning_efforts()` without a catalog or API key, so it always falls back to the static pattern table (o-series / gpt-5* only).

## Fix
When no catalog is passed, `github_model_reasoning_efforts()` resolves the plugin's own Copilot token and reads the existing TTL-cached catalog. Lookup failures are logged at debug and fall back to the static table. This ports the approach of NousResearch/hermes-agent#51953, closed only because Copilot moved into this repo. It also complements #57, which covers Claude's `/v1/messages` route.

## Tests
New `tests/test_copilot_catalog_reasoning.py`: catalog efforts for Claude/Gemini/GPT-6.x with no explicit catalog, clamping in both chat-completions and Responses profiles, offline fallback without raising. `github-copilot` suite: 154 passed.

Verified live: `claude-opus-5.5` with effort `medium` now sends `reasoning.effort=medium`, and Copilot returns 200.

title: yuanbao: strip_cron_wrapper stops matching after the footer-style cron wrapper (hermes-agent#99452)
body:
`strip_cron_wrapper` (`yuanbao/adapter.py:2623`) mirrors the core cron wrapper, and NousResearch/hermes-agent#99452 changes the shape it mirrors: that PR moves the wrapper to a footer so the payload leads, and drops the `To stop or manage this job` line.

```text
before  Cronjob Response: <name>\n(job_id: …)\n-------------\n\n<content>\n\nTo stop or manage…
after   <content>\n\n-------------\nCronjob Response: <name>\n(job_id: …)
```

Ran the plugin's own function — constants and body extracted verbatim from `yuanbao/adapter.py`, not re-typed — against both shapes:

| input | `strip_cron_wrapper` result |
|---|---|
| pre-#99452 (header first) | strips → payload only |
| post-#99452 (payload first) | no-op → message returned unchanged, separator and identifier still in it |

Cause: `content.startswith(CRON_WRAPPER_HEADER_PREFIX)` is false on the first line, so the function returns before doing anything else. Two further anchors go dead:

- `CRON_WRAPPER_DIVIDER` (`"\n-------------\n\n"`) — the new text has `\n-------------\nCronjob Response:`, so that exact substring never occurs;
- `CRON_WRAPPER_FOOTER_PREFIX` (the `To stop or manage…` line) — gone from the wrapper entirely.

Effect for users: every cron delivery arrives with a trailing `-------------` / `Cronjob Response: <name>` / `(job_id: …)` block. Silent, not a crash — the docstring's "unchanged when the shape doesn't match" fallback does its job.

Suggested fix: re-anchor on the payload-first shape — divider `"\n\n-------------\n"`, trailer prefix `"\nCronjob Response: "`, return `content[:divider_pos]` — and keep the legacy constants so an already-queued old-shape message still strips. The comment at `adapter.py:115` names the durable version: import the same key from `cron/scheduler_delivery.py` once that wrapper is keyed.

Context: raised by @teknium1 on NousResearch/hermes-agent#99452 — "The plugin's strip_cron_wrapper must follow the core format; please mention it to the plugin if your format change lands."

title: fix(github-copilot): restore reasoning effort on side tasks routed to the Responses API
body:
Since #74, a side task (title generation, compression, vision, ...) on a Copilot model routed to the Responses API sends no reasoning effort, whatever `reasoning_effort` says, so Copilot runs its default.

Core's auxiliary client sends these models (GPT-5+, except `gpt-5-mini`) through its chat-to-Responses adapter (`CodexAuxiliaryClient`), which reads the effort from `extra_body.reasoning` only. #74 moved `build_api_kwargs_extras` to a top-level `reasoning_effort`: right for `/chat/completions`, but that adapter drops it.

Effort on the wire for a `call_llm` side task configured with `xhigh` (listed by the catalog), against hermes-agent `main` (`fd8a6c41ac`):

| Model | Route | Before #74 | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol` | `/responses` | `reasoning.effort: xhigh` | no `reasoning` field | `reasoning.effort: xhigh` |
| `claude-opus-5.5`, `gemini-4-carbon` | `/chat/completions` | nested `reasoning` (ignored, per #74) | `reasoning_effort: xhigh` | `reasoning_effort: xhigh` |

## Fix

`build_api_kwargs_extras` picks the carrier from the profile's own route, `api_mode_for_model()`, which is what core's auxiliary client routes by: `extra_body.reasoning` for Responses models, top-level `reasoning_effort` for `/chat/completions` models (as in #74). Disabled reasoning keeps #74's rule (`none` only where the model lists it), on the same carrier. Main turns on Responses models go through `reasoning_payload` and are unchanged.

Trade-off: the hook is not told which wire it builds for, so a GPT-5+ model forced onto `/chat/completions` with `model.api_mode` gets the nested field on its main turns again, as before #74.

The offline GPT-5.6/GPT-6 effort table this PR first carried is dropped; #74's live catalog lookup covers it.

## Tests

- New `test_side_task_sends_the_configured_effort` runs a real `call_llm` side task through core's auxiliary client with the HTTP transport stubbed (`offline_side_task` in `conftest.py`, next to `offline_chat_turn`) and reads the effort from the request body, on both routes. On `main`: 1 failed (`gpt-6-luna`), 1 passed.
- Three #74 tests used GPT-5.x ids as `/chat/completions` stand-ins, which Copilot routes to the Responses API. They now use `claude-opus-5.5` and `gpt-5-mini`, or assert the Responses carrier for `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- `python -m pytest -q` in `github-copilot/` against hermes-agent `main` (`fd8a6c41ac`), as CI runs it: 161 passed.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate github-copilot`: passed.

title: github-copilot: /chat/completions ignores nested extra_body.reasoning and drops reasoning_effort for Gemini/Claude models
body:
## Bug Description

On the `github-copilot` plugin (`provider: copilot` / `github-copilot`, `api_mode: chat_completions`), configured `agent.reasoning_effort` has no effect on Copilot `/chat/completions` models (including `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `claude-opus-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-5.5`, etc.) due to **two compounding bugs**:

1. **Wrong wire field on `/chat/completions` (`copilot/__init__.py`)**:
   `CopilotProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras()` returns `({"reasoning": {"effort": effort}}, {})` (`extra_body.reasoning`) instead of `({}, {"reasoning_effort": effort})` (top-level `reasoning_effort`).
   Against the live GitHub Copilot `/chat/completions` endpoint, nested `{"reasoning": {"effort": ...}}` is **silently ignored**, whereas top-level `reasoning_effort` is validated and honored by the backend.
2. **Unresolved catalog capabilities + incomplete offline fallback (`copilot/catalog.py`)**:
   `CopilotProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras()`, `CopilotResponsesMixin.reasoning_payload()` (which also gates `AIAgent._supports_reasoning_extra_body()`), and `setup_reasoning_efforts()` all call `github_model_reasoning_efforts(model)` with `catalog=None` and `api_key=None`.
   `github_model_reasoning_efforts()` only fetches `/models` when `api_key` is explicitly passed (`if catalog is None and api_key:`), falling straight back to `_github_reasoning_efforts_for_model_id()`, which only lists `o1/o3/o4`, `gpt-5*`, and `gpt-6-astra` — returning `[]` for all Gemini (`gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`) and Claude (`claude-opus-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-haiku-5.5`) models.

Note on related issues / PRs:
- Issue #40 and open PRs #65 / #70 track catalog/offline effort lookup, **but both #65 and #70 keep `build_api_kwargs_extras()` emitting `extra_body={"reasoning": {"effort": ...}}`**, which Copilot `/chat/completions` ignores. In addition, resolving credentials inside `github_model_reasoning_efforts()` when `catalog is None` must stay gated on `github_calls_allowed()` so an ambient `GH_TOKEN` on a non-Copilot home never contacts GitHub (`test_activation_gate.py`).
- Also in `build_api_kwargs_extras()`, `reasoning_config={"enabled": False}` (sent by auxiliary tasks such as title generation / compression) previously fell through `reasoning_config.get("effort")` (`None`) to `"medium"` instead of disabling or omitting `reasoning_effort`.

## Live Reproduction Against Copilot `/models` and `/chat/completions`

1. Live `/models` entry for `gemini-4-carbon` (same shape on `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`):
```json
"supports": {
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "reasoning_effort": ["low", "medium", "high"],
  "streaming": true,
  "tool_calls": true,
  "vision": true
},
"supported_endpoints": ["/chat/completions"]
```

2. Probing `POST /chat/completions` on `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com` / `api.githubcopilot.com`:
- Nested `{"reasoning": {"effort": "bogus_invalid"}}` -> **HTTP 200 OK** (silently ignored by server)
- Top-level `{"reasoning_effort": "bogus_invalid"}` -> **HTTP 400 `invalid_reasoning_effort`**:
  ```json
  {"error":{"message":"reasoning_effort \"bogus_invalid\" is not supported by model gemini-4-carbon; supported values: [low medium high]","code":"invalid_reasoning_effort"}}
  ```
  (And on `claude-opus-5.5`: `supported values: [low medium high xhigh max]`.)
- Top-level `{"reasoning_effort": "low"}` vs `{"reasoning_effort": "high"}` on `gemini-4-carbon` scales completion/reasoning output as expected (`comp=175, reasoning_text=0 chars` at `low` vs `comp=1388, reasoning_text=3725 chars` at `high`), and clamping `agent.reasoning_effort: max` -> `"high"` succeeds without HTTP 400.

## Expected Behavior

- `CopilotProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras()` emits top-level `{"reasoning_effort": effort}` (clamped to the model's supported Copilot levels) and handles `enabled: False` cleanly (`"none"` when supported, omitted otherwise).
- `github_model_reasoning_efforts(model)` resolves the active Copilot credential (gated by `github_calls_allowed()` and credential-scoped in `_github_model_catalog_cache`) when `catalog is None`, with offline fallbacks covering Gemini 3.8/4, Claude 5.x, and GPT-5.6/6 tiers when `/models` is unreachable.

title: fix(github-copilot): send top-level reasoning_effort on chat_completions and resolve live catalog efforts
body:
## Summary

Fixes two compounding bugs in `github-copilot` that caused configured `agent.reasoning_effort` to be silently dropped or ignored on Copilot `/chat/completions` models (such as `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `claude-opus-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-haiku-5.5`):

1. **Emit top-level `reasoning_effort` in `CopilotProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras()` (`copilot/__init__.py`)**:
   - Previously returned `({"reasoning": {"effort": effort}}, {})` (`extra_body.reasoning`). Against live `api.githubcopilot.com/chat/completions` and `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/chat/completions`, nested `{"reasoning": {"effort": ...}}` is silently ignored (even bogus values return HTTP 200), whereas top-level `reasoning_effort` is validated and honored (`supported values: [low medium high]` on `gemini-4-carbon`, `[low medium high xhigh max]` on `claude-opus-5.5`).
   - Also handles `reasoning_config={"enabled": False}` from auxiliary tasks cleanly: emits `"none"` only when `"none"` is in the model's supported list, and omits `reasoning_effort` otherwise (Gemini 4 / Claude 5 reject `"none"` with HTTP 400).
   - Note: `CopilotResponsesMixin.reasoning_payload()` (`copilot/responses.py`) keeps returning `{"effort": ...}` for the `/responses` route.

2. **Resolve live `/models` catalog capabilities when `catalog` / `api_key` are omitted + expand offline ladders (`copilot/catalog.py`)**:
   - `build_api_kwargs_extras()`, `reasoning_payload()`, and `setup_reasoning_efforts()` call `github_model_reasoning_efforts(model)` with no `catalog` or `api_key`.
   - When `catalog is None`, resolves `_resolve_copilot_catalog_api_key()` **only when `github_calls_allowed()` is true** (preserving the activation gate so ambient `GH_TOKEN` on non-Copilot homes never contacts GitHub), and passes that key into `fetch_github_model_catalog(api_key=key)` so `_github_model_catalog_cache` remains credential-scoped.
   - Adds offline fallback ladders for `gemini-4*` / `gemini-3.8*` (`["low", "medium", "high"]`) and `claude-{opus,sonnet,haiku}-5*` (`["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]`).

## Test Plan

- [x] Verified regression tests fail on `main` (`21 failed` before fix) and pass with fix (`159 passed` across full `github-copilot` suite).
- [x] `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate github-copilot` passes cleanly.
- [x] Added unit + wire-level tests in `github-copilot/tests/test_copilot_profile.py` covering:
  - Top-level `reasoning_effort` (and absence of `extra_body.reasoning`) on `AIAgent.chat` turns, including `gemini-4-carbon` clamping `max` -> `high`.
  - `enabled: False` behavior when `"none"` is supported vs unsupported.
  - Activation-gated live catalog lookup (`github_calls_allowed()`) + two-credential cache isolation.
  - Offline fallback ladders for Gemini 3.8/4 and Claude 5.x.
- [x] Live-verified against `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com` (`/models` + `/chat/completions`) on `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `claude-opus-5.5`.

Fixes #73
Related: #40, #65, #70

title: fix(github-copilot): send X-GitHub-Api-Version so /models reports the real context window
body:
Copilot's /models returns max_prompt_tokens 200000 for claude-sonnet-5.5 and claude-opus-5.5 (272000 for gpt-6) when the request has no X-GitHub-Api-Version. With X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-08-01 (the Copilot CLI's value) the same Business account reports 936000 (sonnet-5.5) and 1000000 (opus-5.5). I bisected the headers one at a time: only this one changes the limit.

Effect in Hermes: get_copilot_model_context reads /models, so without the header compaction is sized against 200K. Users who pin model.context_length: 1000000 then hit server-side 'prompt budget' errors instead of compacting.

Change: add the header in copilot_request_headers (one constant plus a test assertion). Related core PR for the pin: NousResearch/hermes-agent#133688.

Not verified: I could not reproduce a hard server rejection above 200K with plain /chat/completions (a 667K-token prompt was accepted without the header), so the header fixes the reported limit, and I have not shown it removes every 200K rejection. Tested with the plugin's header tests (3 pass) and a live /models call.

title: Yuanbao: omitted zero business code is rejected as malformed, causing duplicate sends and recovered-reply redelivery
body:
## Summary

After upgrading to Hermes Agent v0.23.1 with the Yuanbao 2.0.0 Labs plugin, a short reply was received multiple times. The plugin reported a malformed send response, retried each chunk up to three times, and sometimes triggered plain-text fallback. Replies marked as failed were also redelivered with the `Recovered reply` prefix.

## Environment / provenance

- Hermes Agent v0.23.1, Docker installation.
- Yuanbao plugin 2.0.0, catalog/install commit `51ede1f023906114ec06c216c4a7b98e8a45d672`.
- The pre-patch local `yuanbao/send_ack.py` was byte-for-byte identical to both that upstream commit and upstream `main` when checked.
- SHA256 of the original file: `81e9577e9fb5c07c63971e7c4d5e5d62a284596d808f5bcac44feea3f0c8b825`.
- No fresh-install reproduction was performed; the comparison rules out a locally modified old ACK parser as the cause in this installation.

## Observed behavior

1. Send a short ordinary reply through the Yuanbao plugin.
2. The recipient sees repeated copies.
3. The sender logs `malformed send response` and attempts 1/3, 2/3, 3/3.
4. Plain-text fallback and recovered-reply delivery can produce additional copies.

A temporary metadata-only diagnostic in the parser exception handler reported:

```text
ACK_DIAG status=0 data_type=bytes data_len=6 parse_error=missing business code
send_text_chunk attempt 1/3 failed: malformed send response
send_text_chunk attempt 2/3 failed: malformed send response
send_text_chunk attempt 3/3 failed: malformed send response
```

No raw live payload, conversation text, credentials, message IDs, or account identifiers are included. The real payload bytes were not captured; the diagnostic establishes that parsing reached the missing-business-code check rather than a truncation exception.

## Suspected cause

`decode_send_ack_payload()` initializes `code = None` and raises if field 1 is absent:

```python
if code is None:
    raise ValueError("missing business code")
return code, message
```

This rejects an otherwise parseable response whose zero-valued scalar code is omitted. Under protobuf default-value semantics, omission can represent zero. Maintainers should confirm the exact response schema; `head.status == 0` alone should not override an explicit nonzero business error.

## Minimal synthetic regression fixture

This is synthetic test data, NOT the captured six-byte live payload. Place the assertion in the plugin's existing test harness with its normal import of `ack_from_response`:

```python
# field 2: empty string; field 1 (zero code) omitted
response = {"head": {"status": 0}, "data": b"\x12\x00"}
assert ack_from_response("Yuanbao", response)["success"] is True
```

The assertion fails with the original code and passes with the local change below.

## Local workaround and verification

```diff
-    if code is None:
-        raise ValueError("missing business code")
-    return code, message
+    return 0 if code is None else code, message
```

Ten synthetic offline cases passed: omitted zero code, explicit zero code, nonzero business code 999, nonzero transport status, truncated varint, truncated length-delimited field, unsupported wire type, truncated fixed-width field, incorrect data type, and empty payload. Negative cases remained failures.

After applying the change and restarting the gateway, the recipient confirmed a short test reply arrived once. This is a limited end-to-end check, not exhaustive validation of long messages, attachments, all malformed protobuf inputs, or delivery-ledger behavior.

## Expected behavior

Accept schema-valid ACKs that omit the default zero business code, preserve rejection of explicit nonzero business errors and malformed payloads, and avoid retrying already-delivered messages solely because the zero code was omitted. Please add a regression test for omitted-code ACKs.

title: fix: retain Copilot pool grants during runtime renewal
body:
## Summary

Keep the durable GitHub grant in Copilot pool rows and exchange only the selected row. The exchanged bearer and endpoint go back to core as a `PoolRuntimeCredential` instead of overwriting `entry.access_token` and `entry.base_url` (the corruption in NousResearch/hermes-agent#155441).

`refresh_pool_runtime_credentials` renews only the failed row's grant and never substitutes an ambient account or the raw grant. Initial resolution keeps the existing same-account raw fallback; catalog source ordering is unchanged.

## Changes

- Seed env rows with the raw grant; `prepare_pool_entry` exchanges at selection and returns a typed pair.
- `refresh_pool_runtime_credentials`: exact-row renewal. A fine-grained PAT is declined before any cache eviction or exchange; it is the bearer itself and is never exchanged.
- `api_mode_for_model` reads the catalog with a pooled grant's exchanged bearer. Core resolves a row's api_mode before preparing it, so it otherwise received the raw grant.
- `credential_pool_base_urls` lists the four official `*.githubcopilot.com` origins. Relays, ports, paths and lookalikes are refused at selection and at renewal.
- Feature-detect the SDK: on an older core the plugin stays inactive and logs one warning.
- Tests: persistence/reload, selected-only exchange, refused routes, PAT decline, and an offline 401-recovery harness for `copilot` and `github-copilot` with one and two rows, adapted from @recoilburner's review on NousResearch/hermes-agent#154360.

## Before this leaves Draft

1. **Core SDK:** NousResearch/hermes-agent#154360 (`PoolRuntimeCredential`, `refresh_pool_runtime_credentials`, `credential_pool_base_urls`) must land first. No catalog repin before a compatible core release.
2. **GHEC pool rows:** `copilot-api.<enterprise>.ghe.com` can't be listed in a static `credential_pool_base_urls`, so core refuses that endpoint for a `hermes auth add copilot` row. With only `COPILOT_GH_HOST` set, the request then goes to `api.githubcopilot.com` with the GHEC bearer; with `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL` or `model.base_url` set it reaches GHEC but isn't renewed after a 401. (On `main` such rows reach GHEC, but the exchanged bearer overwrites the saved grant.) The env-token setup (`COPILOT_GH_HOST` + `COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`) keeps working through core's env path and re-exchanges after a 401. Fixing this needs core to accept one exact per-user origin for the profile; asked on NousResearch/hermes-agent#154360. The README documents the gap, and tests pin that neither selection nor renewal moves a row to an unlisted origin.

The `github-copilot` spelling recovers only once core keeps the pool for a declared alias: NousResearch/hermes-agent#160726. Without it those four cases skip; the gate probes `credential_pool_matches_provider`, not a version. The replay track (#78, landed via #99; core NousResearch/hermes-agent#154361) is independent.

A grant that an older derived bearer already overwrote can't be recovered; that account must sign in again. No installed plugin, account or profile changes here.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` at `af1cb017`. One conflict, in `seed_pool_credentials`: kept the raw-grant seeding; #55's PAT guard in `prepare_pool_entry` and #96's auxiliary refresh came through unchanged.

Plugin head `ee9740c`, offline, synthetic credentials, isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME, Python 3.14.9:
- Against NousResearch/hermes-agent#154360 at `75e5f9b6f0` merged with NousResearch/hermes-agent#160726 at `4e0ef61261`: **342 passed**; manifest validation passed.
- Against NousResearch/hermes-agent#154360 at `75e5f9b6f0` alone: 338 passed, 4 skipped (the `github-copilot` cases).
- Unchanged `main` plugin suite on the same core: 306 passed.

From `github-copilot/`:

```bash
HERMES_AGENT_REPO="$CORE" PYTHONPATH="$CORE" "$HERMES_PYTHON" -m pytest -q
```

## CI

The workflow checks out core `main`, which lacks the SDK, so the three Copilot jobs stop at manifest validation (`registered no ProviderProfile at import`) before pytest. This is the dependency gate, not a test failure; no test or validator was weakened to get past it.

title: fix: classify Copilot connection-bound replay rejections
body:
## Summary

Classify only Copilot's HTTP 401 message `input item does not belong to this connection` as invalid encrypted content, rather than an authentication failure. Mark it non-rotating and non-fallback so core can repair the rejected request without treating the account as exhausted.

Related issue: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins/issues/42

Provider-specific classification stays in `copilot/responses.py`, following the [ownership guidance](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70486#issuecomment-6412844739).

## Changes

- Inspect the actual error message and HTTP status through the existing profile classification hook.
- Exclude this narrow rejection from stale-credential renewal.
- Retain genuine token expiry, ordinary authentication failure and stale-integrator handling.
- Cover unrelated messages/statuses, malformed bodies, non-message fields and provider/host scoping.

No proactive replay stripping, credential resolver change or new pool SDK dependency is introduced. The rebase preserves upstream's current reasoning payload and live-catalog behavior.

## Required core companion and release ordering

**Ship https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/154361 (`fix: repair classified encrypted replay before auth recovery`) before distributing this plugin classification update.** Both changes are required for complete rejection repair: this PR classifies the provider-specific rejection; the companion performs bounded, request-attributed repair before authentication recovery. Passing plugin checks against core main does not establish that the companion recovery is available there.

The independent pool track is https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/154360 and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins/pull/77; neither is a dependency of this classification change. If the two core PRs land separately, preserve classified-replay-before-auth handling and scoped-pool-or-legacy-profile selection when reconciling their shared recovery files. Earlier combined-track validation is historical, not a fresh integrated run on these rebased heads.

Any later catalog distribution must pin an actual merged Labs revision. This PR changes no catalog pin, installed plugin or saved account.

## How to test

Set `CORE` to an absolute compatible core checkout and `HERMES_PYTHON` to its managed test interpreter. From `github-copilot/`, using an isolated home and cleared ambient credentials:

```bash
HERMES_AGENT_REPO="$CORE" PYTHONPATH="$CORE" "$HERMES_PYTHON" -m pytest -q
PYTHONPATH="$CORE" "$HERMES_PYTHON" -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate .
```

Core must be on `PYTHONPATH`; the standalone plugin does not supply the `providers` package.

## Current validation

Labs head `e8b071277e9f7b67e0aa32e05a753b8088993cf9` is rebased onto upstream Labs main `46f6da9af0c4e9ad5a3c9444dfecfa5bf7debf76`. The fix was not already upstream. Rebase was conflict-free and `git range-diff` confirms the original patch is unchanged; `git diff --check` passes.

- Full plugin suite against the local rebased companion core snapshot `38279951d45d17ca1c724c99eb453af16ba2d044` (base `d1b46d718ffe675427928eff7e5fff69bcb4519b`): **182 passed**, no skips; plugin validation passed.
- Full plugin suite against upstream core snapshot `d1b46d718ffe675427928eff7e5fff69bcb4519b`: **182 passed**, no skips; plugin validation passed. This is classification compatibility, not proof of companion recovery on upstream core.

These are separate runs of the same suite, not an additive test total. The local companion snapshot identifies exactly what was exercised; it does not assert the companion PR's eventual rebased publication SHA. Existing `copilot-acp` live-client isolation remains in-process only.

The original intermittent live rejection was not reproduced. Local tests use synthetic offline errors; no live-provider reproduction or whole-core-suite pass is claimed.
