title: fix(copilot): keep an exchange lock's table entry while callers hold it (#107)
body:
Fixes #107.

## Problem

When pruning the Copilot exchange-lock table, an entry was dropped as soon as its lock was
*unlocked* — but a caller that has just been handed the lock (`with _exchange_lock_for(fp):`)
has not acquired it yet, and a waiter queued behind the holder has not acquired it at all.
Evicting the entry in that window let the next lookup mint a **second** lock for the same
token, so two exchanges could run concurrently: single-flight broken, redundant token burns
(exactly what #51's single-flight was built to prevent).

The issue's source-level probe reproduces on `main` (`a is b: False`); with this change the
same probe returns `a is b: True`.

## Fix

Exchange locks are now small lease objects:

- `_exchange_lock_for` counts each handout (`refs`) atomically with the get-or-create;
- a new `_exchange_lock_lease(fp)` context manager — now the single production acquire path —
  acquires the lock and releases the handout in `finally` (also on exception);
- `_prune_exchange_caches` keeps an entry while `refs > 0` **or** the underlying lock is held;
  an entry whose last handout is released is prunable again, so the #51 bound still applies.

No lock ordering is introduced: the guard and the inner lock are never held at the same time
(handout and release take the guard alone; acquire/release of the inner lock happens outside it).

## Tests

`tests/test_exchange_cache_bounded.py` — 11 passed (6 new):
- handed-out-unacquired lock survives a 64-entry prune flood (the #107 repro);
- waiter pin (handout on a locked fingerprint) survives pruning;
- released entry becomes prunable again;
- `_exchange_lock_lease` pins the entry for its whole scope and balances refs;
- release on exception (refs back to 0, lock unlocked);
- table stays bounded after 200 handout/release cycles.

Neighbours: `test_copilot_token_exchange.py` + `test_copilot_pool_exchange.py` +
`test_copilot_auth_bounded_reads.py` — 21 passed. `ruff check` clean on both touched files.

title: [Discussion]: Move the github-copilot plugin to the official Copilot SDK (or add an SDK-based provider)?
body:
## Summary

Is there interest in building on the official Copilot SDK (now `microsoft/copilot-sdk`; PyPI `microsoft-copilot-sdk` 2.0.3, Python >=3.11), either by migrating the existing `copilot` provider or by adding a separate SDK-based provider alongside it? Opening this to gauge interest and discuss design before anyone writes code.

## Why

The current provider works well, but it's built on an undocumented surface and can't reach newer Copilot features that ship through the SDK/CLI.

- **Supported auth and transport.** The provider exchanges a GitHub token at `api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` (undocumented) and sends CLI-mimicking headers to `api.githubcopilot.com`. Several open issues live in that layer and could be removed or reduced by a supported auth path:
  - #43 — exchange endpoint returns 404 for Individual Pro subscribers
  - #48 — `gho_` OAuth tokens rejected as PATs on Windows
  - #107 — exchange-lock pruning can replace a lock a caller holds
  - #87 — token refresh/setup flows ignore credential pool/priority (token lifecycle would move to the SDK; multi-account pooling would remain Hermes-side)

  The SDK officially supports `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`, OAuth-app tokens, CLI login, and BYOK.
- **Wire-level quirks.** #42 (Responses replays connection-bound encrypted reasoning) and #56 (Claude on `/chat/completions` ignores `cache_ttl` / hides cache writes) exist because the plugin selects and drives each wire format itself. With the SDK, wire selection belongs to the runtime; worth verifying whether both resolve.
- **Copilot Fusion.** [Fusion](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/copilot-fusion) is the successor to auto model selection and HydraFusion ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-route-and-orchestrate-models-with-github-copilot-fusion/)): it picks an execution pattern (single, cascade, or multi-model critique) and the models for each request. The SDK exposes it as `model="fusion"` with effort tiers `standard` / `high` / `max`. Related: auto-mode recovery can retry a request on automatic routing after `model_degraded`, `model_overloaded`, or a per-model rate limit.
- **Usage and cost reporting.** Per-call `assistant.usage` events report model plus input/output/cache-read/cache-write tokens, including sub-agent calls and Fusion's routed models; plus `session.usage.getMetrics`, per-model AI-credit pricing via `models.list`, and `account.getQuota`. With Copilot's token-based billing in AI credits ([models and pricing](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing)), authoritative per-call model and token data would make cost reporting more accurate (cf. #58).
- **Tracking upstream.** New models, routing, and runtime features would arrive via SDK releases rather than being reverse-engineered from CLI traffic.

## The design question

The SDK is the Copilot agent runtime, not a chat-completions client — but nearly every part of its agent loop is host-overridable:

- **Tools:** `mode="empty"` plus `available_tools` / `excluded_tools` (via `ToolSet`) disables built-ins entirely; host tools are registered with `define_tool`, replaceable mid-session (`set_tools`); individual built-ins can be overridden (`overrides_built_in_tool`).
- **System prompt:** `system_message` supports `append`, full replace, or `customize` (per-section replace/remove/append/prepend).
- **Hooks:** `on_pre_tool_use` (allow/deny/modify), `on_post_tool_use`, user-prompt submitted/transformed, session start/end, error handling.
- **Permissions and input:** permission handlers, user-input requests, elicitation.
- **Steering and queueing:** mid-turn steering and enqueued follow-ups.
- **Context:** infinite sessions with compaction, context-clearing tools, session persistence/resume.
- **Models:** `set_model` mid-session, reasoning effort, BYOK custom providers.

So the question is less "can Hermes control it" and more how much of Hermes's own loop to delegate, and whether to replace the current provider or sit beside it.

Loop arrangement:

- **A. Hermes-controlled loop, SDK as model backend.** Empty mode with no built-ins, Hermes's system prompt (replace mode), and Hermes's tools registered as SDK tools whose handlers dispatch into Hermes's tool execution. Map SDK events (message deltas, `assistant.usage`, `session.idle`) onto Hermes's streaming and usage interfaces. Open question: run each Hermes turn as one SDK turn with tool calls via handlers, or can a turn yield tool calls back to Hermes? That determines how Hermes's approvals, compression, delegation, and trajectory recording integrate (hooks and permission handlers look like the natural seam for approvals).
- **B. Hybrid.** Hermes keeps its loop for normal turns; specific features (e.g. Fusion) route through the SDK.

Delivery:

1. **Migrate.** Rebuild the existing `copilot` provider on the SDK. One code path; resolves the auth/transport issues above; bigger change and risk for existing users.
2. **Coexist.** Add a separate provider (e.g. `copilot-sdk`), in this plugin or its own, alongside the current `copilot` provider. Opt-in, no disruption to current users, allows side-by-side comparison; a later migration becomes an easy call if it proves out. Cost: two Copilot providers to maintain in the meantime.
3. **Status quo + direct-API probe.** If `api.githubcopilot.com` accepts `model: "fusion"` directly, the current provider could add Fusion without the SDK. Doesn't address the auth/transport/cost-reporting points above.

## Considerations

- **Runtime packaging:** SDK v2 defaults to loading a native Rust runtime in-process (C ABI; no crash isolation). It also supports a spawned child process (stdio/TCP) or attaching to a standalone `copilot-runtime --server`, probably a better fit for long-running gateways. Python downloads the runtime artifacts; the Copilot CLI need not be installed.
- **Churn:** the SDK is mid-rename (GitHub → Microsoft). Package and namespace names may move, and several usage/quota RPCs are marked experimental, so pinning SDK + runtime versions would matter.
- **Cost reporting:** Fusion bills each routed model at its standard rate, so per-call usage data is what cost reporting needs. Per-call spend is reported as `copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu` (see findings in the comments); `assistant.usage.cost` is the legacy per-request multiplier and can be ignored.
- **Auto-mode recovery** requires the app to surface a consent offer; headless gateways need a policy (auto-accept, decline, or configurable).
- **Scope:** this concerns the `copilot` API provider only.¹

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is building on the SDK something you'd consider — migrate (1), coexist (2), or neither?
2. If yes, which loop arrangement (A or B) would you accept?
3. If coexisting, should it live in this plugin or a separate one?
4. Any blockers (packaging, the native runtime, licensing) that would rule it out?

## References

- https://github.com/microsoft/copilot-sdk (README → Architecture; `python/README.md` → Auto routing tiers, System Message Customization, Session Hooks, Permission Handling, Infinite Sessions)
- SDK docs: `docs/features/agent-loop.md`, `changing-tools.md`, `steering-and-queueing.md`, `usage-and-billing.md`, `auto-mode-recovery.md`, `session-persistence.md` (Copilot Fusion names), `docs/hooks/`
- About Copilot Fusion: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/copilot-fusion
- Fusion GA changelog: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-route-and-orchestrate-models-with-github-copilot-fusion/
- Copilot models and pricing: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing
- Related issues: #42, #43, #48, #56, #58, #87, #107

¹ The plugin's other provider, `copilot-acp`, drives the Copilot CLI over ACP. It's even less featured than the direct API provider (no native tool calls, no real streaming, no usage data), so it isn't a substitute here.

title: Make Editor-Version / Editor-Plugin-Version configurable; hardcoded vscode/1.104.1 is rejected by a corporate Copilot proxy
body:
Repo: NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins (plugin: github-copilot, v1.0.1)

Summary
On an enterprise Copilot plan behind a corporate Copilot proxy, chat requests from the plugin are rejected with a reply along the lines of:

Copilot Chat plugin is too old, please update Visual Studio Code to Version 1.88+ and Copilot Chat plugin to version copilot-chat/0.14.0 or higher. VersionInfo: vscode/1.104.1 | HermesAgent/1.0

The reply comes back as a normal chat response (HTTP 200, streamed), so Hermes shows it as the model's answer instead of raising an error.

Cause
The plugin hardcodes the editor identity in copilot/credentials.py:

```
_EDITOR_VERSION = "vscode/1.104.1"
no Editor-Plugin-Version header is sent on chat requests
```
The proxy checks both the editor version and the Copilot Chat extension version. Both values are fixed in the source, so they can't be changed without editing the installed plugin.

Reproduce
Enterprise Copilot account behind a proxy that enforces minimum client versions.
```
hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#github-copilot
hermes auth add copilot, then hermes chat --provider copilot --model claude-haiku-5.5 -q "Reply with exactly: COPILOT_OK"
```
The "plugin is too old" message comes back instead of COPILOT_OK.
What fixed it for me
```
--- a/copilot/credentials.py
+++ b/copilot/credentials.py
@@ -191,7 +191,7 @@
-_EDITOR_VERSION = "vscode/1.104.1"
+_EDITOR_VERSION = "vscode/1.148.0"
@@ -523,6 +523,7 @@
         "Editor-Version": _PAT_EDITOR_VERSION if is_pat else _EDITOR_VERSION,
+        "Editor-Plugin-Version": "copilot-chat/0.26.7",
         "User-Agent": "HermesAgent/1.0",
```
With these two changes (and a gateway restart), the same command returns COPILOT_OK. A direct API request with those two headers also returned a normal reply.

Request
Let users override the editor version and the extension version, e.g. COPILOT_EDITOR_VERSION and COPILOT_PLUGIN_VERSION env vars (read via get_secret like COPILOT_GH_HOST), with the current values as defaults.
Send Editor-Plugin-Version on chat requests by default.
Optional: treat a response body matching "plugin is too old" as an error, so it isn't shown as an assistant message.
Notes
Hermes v0.23.4, Linux.
Provider plugins run from frozen snapshots under runtime/provider-plugins/, and stale .pyc files kept the old constant until I deleted them. Worth knowing when testing edits.
Separate from this issue: in environments with TLS interception, SSL_CERT_FILE must point at a bundle that includes the system CAs, because a single CA file breaks api.github.com.





GitHub Copilot Enterprise with Hermes: what I did
1. Installed the plugin and signed in

Ran hermes plugins install github-copilot. Copilot is no longer in Hermes core, so it ships as a plugin.
hermes auth add copilot needs an interactive terminal, so I ran the plugin's device-code login function in the background. You entered the code at github.com/login/device.
The GitHub token is saved as COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in ~/.hermes/.env (mode 600). It persists across reboots.
2. Fixed TLS (first blocker)

Enterprise routes api.githubcopilot.com and api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com through a TLS-intercepting proxy (copilotproxy.mycompany.com). Hermes' Python didn't trust the company CA, so every request failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
Pointing SSL_CERT_FILE at company-CA.pem alone broke api.github.com, because it replaces the whole trust store.
I built a combined bundle at ~/.hermes/certs/ca-bundle.pem (system CAs plus the company CA).
systemctl --user set-environment failed on your machine, so I added a systemd drop-in at ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-gateway.service.d/ssl-ca.conf that sets SSL_CERT_FILE for the gateway.
3. Fixed the version rejection (second blocker)

The company proxy answered "Copilot Chat plugin is too old". The plugin sent vscode/1.104.1 and no extension version.
I changed _EDITOR_VERSION to vscode/1.148.0 (your VS Code version) and added the header Editor-Plugin-Version: copilot-chat/0.26.7 in copilot/credentials.py. A direct API test with those headers returned a real reply.
4. Cleared caches

Hermes runs plugins from frozen snapshots in ~/.hermes/runtime/provider-plugins/, and compiled .pyc files kept the old version string. I deleted the plugin's .pyc files and you restarted the gateway so it took a fresh snapshot.
5. Verified

hermes chat --provider copilot --model claude-haiku-5.5 returned COPILOT_OK.

title: fix(github-copilot): keep live model catalog reachable with plan hosts
body:
## Summary

Keep the live Copilot model catalog reachable when a Copilot plan host is
configured in `model.base_url`.

## Root Cause

`hermes_cli.models._configured_relay_base_url()` treats any configured
`model.base_url` that differs from the provider profile URL as a relay.
`_RELAY_AWARE_CATALOG_FETCHERS` does not include `copilot`, so
`provider_model_ids()` skips this plugin's `picker_catalog` hook and returns
the curated list marked as a fallback.

Copilot plan hosts such as `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` are first-party
endpoints, not user relays. Bypassing the relay check returned 30 current
models in about one second, versus 17 stale models in zero seconds with the
check in place.

## Fix

- Register `copilot` in core's `_RELAY_AWARE_CATALOG_FETCHERS` when this
  plugin is active.
- Read the constant defensively: core can import the plugin while
  `hermes_cli.models` is still initializing, so a missing attribute must
  never fail provider registration.
- Add regression tests for the opt-in and for the live hook being called
  with a plan host configured.

## How to Verify

1. Set `model.provider: copilot` and `model.base_url` to a Copilot plan host.
2. Open Desktop settings, then Models, and press "Refresh models".
3. The list should contain current models such as `gpt-6.2-sol`,
   `claude-fable-5.2`, and `gemini-4-neon` rather than the 17 curated entries.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression tests in `tests/test_relay_aware_catalog.py`
- [x] Full upstream suite passes: 308 passed
- [ ] Manual verification with a plan host configured

## Risk Assessment

Low. The change adds one provider id to a discovery opt-in list. It does not
alter inference routing, credentials, or request headers. On a core without
that constant the hook is a no-op.

title: fix(github-copilot): reject boolean values as context window limits
body:
## Summary

Reject boolean values when reading Copilot model context window limits.

## Root Cause

`bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python. The existing check

```python
isinstance(window, int) and window > 0
```

therefore accepts `True` as a limit of one token and `False` as a failed
check. A malformed catalog payload can set a model's context window to 1.

Both `max_context_window_tokens` and its `max_prompt_tokens` fallback use
the same check, so a boolean in either field is accepted.

## Fix

Reject `bool` explicitly in both checks with
`not isinstance(window, bool)`, while preserving the
`max_context_window_tokens` to `max_prompt_tokens` fallback order.

Add two regression tests: a boolean preferred field must fall back to the
prompt cap, and a boolean prompt cap with no valid alternative must yield
`None`.

## How to Verify

1. Feed a catalog payload with `max_context_window_tokens: true` into
   `get_copilot_model_context()`.
2. The boolean must be ignored and the fallback field used.
3. Repeat with a boolean in `max_prompt_tokens`; the result must be `None`.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression tests in `tests/test_copilot_context_window.py`
- [x] Full upstream suite passes: 308 passed
- [ ] Manual verification not required (pure parsing change)

## Risk Assessment

Low. Only rejects values that are not meaningful token counts. Valid integer
limits keep the existing behavior.

title: `github-copilot` alias leaves the Desktop model picker empty
body:
### Description

Hermes Desktop's settings page shows the provider selector but no model
selector when `model.provider` is set to `github-copilot` (a documented
alias). The same page works with `copilot`.

Inference itself is unaffected: core normalizes the alias correctly. Only
the picker is affected, so the default model cannot be switched from the GUI.

### Root cause

The settings page resolves the catalog row with
`findCatalogProvider(providers, selectedProvider)`, matching on `slug`,
`name`, or `aliases`. The inventory rows built by
`hermes_cli.model_switch_providers.add_builtin_row()` do not contain an
`aliases` field. The Copilot row is:

- `slug`: `copilot`
- `name`: `GitHub Copilot`
- `aliases`: absent

`github-copilot` matches none of them, so `selectedProviderRow` becomes
`null`, `needsSetup` becomes true, and the model control is replaced by a
"set up provider" action.

This lives in hermes-agent core / Desktop, not in this plugin. The plugin
only exposes the profile and its aliases.

### Workaround for users

Use the canonical name in config.yaml:

```yaml
model:
  provider: copilot
```

Normal user flows already write this value: `hermes model` hard-codes
`provider_id = "copilot"`, and the Desktop settings page saves the catalog
row's slug (`copilot`). The alias only appears when a config file is written
or restored manually.

### Suggested fix

Either include the profile aliases in inventory rows, or normalize
`selectedProvider` before `findCatalogProvider()` in Desktop. A plugin-side
workaround is possible but would mean patching core internals, so it is not
proposed here.

### Environment

- hermes-agent after Copilot was removed from core
- github-copilot plugin installed from the Labs repo
- `model.base_url` set to a Copilot plan host (see separate PR draft)

title: fix(yuanbao): strings keep core's language aliases and profile locale overrides
body:
Same gap @unsupportedpastels found in DingTalk (#108, bce93d1): `yuanbao/_i18n.py` replaced core's catalog instead of falling back to it.

- `HERMES_LANGUAGE=jp` / `deutsch` (aliases core accepts) fell through to English.
- A profile's `locales/<lang>.yaml` override for `platform.yuanbao.*` was ignored.

Fix (Mark's patch shape, credited via Co-authored-by): `t()` asks `agent.i18n.t` first (overlay > packs > bundled) and uses the plugin's bundled texts only on a core miss; `language()` resolves through `resolve_language_id`.

Tests: Mark's three tests ported to yuanbao — all 3 fail on main, pass with the fix; full yuanbao suite 306 passed against core main (ab7e19a).

Touches only `yuanbao/_i18n.py` and `yuanbao/tests/test_plugin_packaging.py`; no overlap with #114 (`register.py`, `test_yuanbao_plugin_registration.py`).
